memories.memory_text: I saw the Shiite peasants piling into the trucks, and I helped make sure Imam and his daughter got in safely before I joined them in the back of the crowded truck, where I sat with a smile.

grounded_facts: The convoy, led by Archie in the Humvee, departs along the desert road toward the border.
memories.memory_text: I watched as Archie whistled from the Humvee and led the convoy out, and I could see our trucks rolling along the desert road toward the border.

grounded_facts: Archie proposes and initiates a plan to escort the Shiites on foot to the Iranian side of the border.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie that we'd be walking the Shiites on foot to the Iranian side of the border, then returning to the trucks.

grounded_facts: Doc turns and signals for the drivers to move their vehicles forward in preparation for the operation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc turn and signal for the drivers to move their vehicles forward in preparation for the operation.

grounded_facts: Troy disengages the safety on his M-16 rifle, indicating preparation for potential conflict.
memories.memory_text: I disengaged the safety on my M-16 rifle to prepare in case we encountered any threats during the crossing.

grounded_facts: U.S. drivers exit their vehicles with rifles ready and disengage safeties, assuming defensive posture.
memories.memory_text: I saw the U.S. drivers get out of their vehicles with rifles ready and disengage the safeties, taking up a defensive posture.

grounded_facts: Archie instructs the group to form a close group before crossing the border, which is then translated by the Imam.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie tell the group to make a close formation before crossing, and then the Imam translated it so everyone would understand.

grounded_facts: The group of Shiites, carrying Vig's body and flanked by U.S. drivers including Archie, Troy, and Doc, passes through a narrow opening in the razor wire at the border and continues walking on the other side.
A coordinated movement of Shiite refugees and U.S. drivers crossing the border through a narrow opening in razor wire, carrying Vig's body and maintaining armed vigilance.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the group that moved through a narrow opening in the razor wire at the border, carrying Vig's body, with me and the other U.S. drivers flanking the Shiites and keeping our rifles ready as we spread out on the other side.

grounded_facts: Doc initially misinterprets Troy's issue as mechanical ('Let the air out') but then tells him to stay back upon realizing it's a health issue.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc tell me to let the air out at first, but then he realized something was wrong and told me to stay back.

grounded_facts: Troy suddenly drops to one knee and reports feeling dizzy, despite Doc suspecting a tire issue at first; he insists he is all right but appears unwell.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly dropped to one knee and felt dizzy, and when I told Doc it wasn't the air, I insisted I was all right even though I didn't know what was wrong.

grounded_facts: Captain Van Meter verbally attacks Troy during arrest, rejecting his pleas and asserting mission detachment.
memories.memory_text: I pleaded with Captain Van Meter during the arrest, but he shouted at me, telling me to shut my goddamn mouth and that I was fucked now.

grounded_facts: Troy, unable to breathe due to tight restraints, has his plastic cuffs cut by a sympathetic soldier, allowing him to access his chest valve and breathe.
A U.S. soldier silently cuts Troy's cuffs, defying orders to save his life.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't breathe with my hands cuffed behind my back, and I knew I needed to reach my chest valve, but I couldn't move — then a U.S. soldier cut my cuffs without saying a word, and I managed to turn the valve and finally get air.

grounded_facts: Archie reveals the presence of stolen Kuwaiti gold bullion to General Horn, proving its recovery by the group.
memories.memory_text: I saw the MP knock over the barrel and spill the gold bars onto the sand while Doc and I were held back, and I watched the General look at it as we stood in custody.

grounded_facts: Archie appeals to General Horn's sense of honor and ambition to save the Shiites, offering the gold as leverage.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie tell General Horn that he made a deal based on soldier's honor and that returning the gold could make him a hero, hoping it would save the Shiites.

grounded_facts: Archie, Troy, and Doc are apprehended and handcuffed by U.S. Military Police upon arrival of U.S. forces.
memories.memory_text: I was grabbed by MPs when we arrived, and even though I tried to pull away, they cuffed me and held me there with Archie and Doc while we watched everything go down.

grounded_facts: General Horn intervenes with Iraqi forces, stopping the imminent execution of the Shiite refugees.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Horn fire his pistol into the air, and the Iraqi soldiers froze just as they were about to execute the Shiites; then I watched him walk over and speak with their general to stop the killing.

grounded_facts: General Horn orders the confiscation of news cameras and tapes, suppressing documentation of the event.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Horn shut down the cameras—first yelling at the journalist, then smashing the camera, and finally having the MPs take the tapes so nothing could be documented.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers release the Shiite refugees, who then cross the border into Iran and are received by relief workers.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldiers release the Shiite refugees, and I watched them cross the border into Iran where relief workers were waiting to receive them.

grounded_facts: Six Apache helicopters arrive and land between Archie and the border, blocking passage and creating chaos with dust and noise.
memories.memory_text: I saw six Apache helicopters approaching and then landing right between us and the border, kicking up dust and noise everywhere, and then U.S. troops poured out and blocked our way completely, making it impossible to move forward.

grounded_facts: A group of U.S. soldiers and Shiite refugees attempt to cross the Iraqi border into Iran, culminating in confrontation with U.S. military forces.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to cross the border with Archie, Doc, and the Shiite refugees when everything went sideways — the U.S. military showed up and started grabbing us, pulling me away from the group, and I watched as the Iraqi soldiers took the Shiites prisoner before they were finally released and walked across the border while I stood there in cuffs.

grounded_facts: U.S. soldiers begin whistling and clapping in support of Archie, Troy, and Doc despite their arrest.
memories.memory_text: Even though we were under arrest, I heard a soldier start whistling, then another joined in with clapping, and soon all the U.S. soldiers around us were cheering for me, Archie, and Doc.

grounded_facts: Imam and his daughter wave from the Iranian side as they board a Red Crescent bus, with Archie, Troy, and Doc waving back in handcuffs.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there in handcuffs with Archie and Doc when I saw Imam and his daughter wave from the Iranian side as they got onto a Red Crescent bus, so I raised my cuffed hands to wave back.

grounded_facts: Troy directs workers in handling carpet rolls, demonstrating managerial role.
memories.memory_text: I gave instructions to the workers as they carried out the big rolls of carpet, making sure everything moved smoothly.

grounded_facts: Troy uses a respiratory inhaler, indicating a health condition requiring medical management.
memories.memory_text: I used my inhaler during the day because I could feel my breathing acting up again.

grounded_facts: A workday scene at Troy's carpet business where operational activities are underway.
memories.memory_text: I was running things at my carpet business that day, with workers moving inventory and someone even turning down my offer to partner up.

grounded_facts: Troy asks whether they are authorized to shoot the Iraqi soldier, showing uncertainty and deferring to others for guidance.
memories.memory_text: I asked the others if we were supposed to shoot that guy or not—I didn't know the answer and was trying to find out what to do.

grounded_facts: Captain Van Meter provides a vague and logically circular rule of engagement regarding when to shoot surrendering enemies.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Captain Van Meter that if the enemy surrenders, don't shoot, but if they don't surrender, then shoot—it didn't help clear up the confusion.

grounded_facts: After the shooting, Soldier #3 makes a racially charged remark identifying the dead soldier as a 'towel head'.
memories.memory_text: After I shot him, I heard one of the other soldiers say, 'That guy just shot a towel head,' and I knew they were talking about me.

grounded_facts: After receiving ambiguous orders, Troy aims and shoots an Iraqi soldier who had waved a white flag and then picked up a gun.
memories.memory_text: I aimed my rifle at the Iraqi soldier after getting unclear orders, saw him with both a flag and a rifle, and I shot him—watched his neck explode and then stood there looking down at his body.

grounded_facts: A tense standoff and subsequent shooting occurs at a sand berm in the Iraqi desert involving U.S. soldiers and an Iraqi soldier.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldier on the berm, raised my rifle, and later saw him on the ground, neck blown open, still holding both a flag and a gun while looking up at me.

grounded_facts: A soldier compares the scene to the movie 'Predator', specifically the scene where Carl Weathers' arm keeps firing after being shot off.
memories.memory_text: I heard a soldier say it was just like 'Predator,' where Carl Weathers' arm gets shot off and his hand keeps firing when it hits the ground.

grounded_facts: Troy reports a sudden and severe headache, indicating a possible physical or psychological shift.
memories.memory_text: I got a really bad headache all of a sudden--

grounded_facts: Soldiers gather around the dead Iraqi to view and photograph the body, treating it as a spectacle.
memories.memory_text: I saw the other soldiers gather around the body and start taking pictures, even as I walked away holding my temple because of the pain.

grounded_facts: Troy states the price for taking pictures with the corpse.
Troy monetizes access to the dead Iraqi by charging soldiers for pictures.
memories.memory_text: I set the price at twenty bucks for photos with the corpse, and I saw the soldiers pull out their cash and pay me for the chance to take pictures.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi individual dies, marking a key event in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi die right there, his breathing just stopped.

grounded_facts: Troy is paraded on soldiers' shoulders in a celebratory, ritualistic manner while holding up a Coke and a Bud can like torches, amid loud music and chaotic energy.
memories.memory_text: I was lifted up on the soldiers' shoulders, wearing a headdress, holding my Coke and Bud cans high like torches while the music blasted around me.

grounded_facts: An informal, high-energy gathering of soldiers in a tent involving music, performance, and physical play, blending patriotism, aggression, and release.
memories.memory_text: I saw the whole tent go wild with music, Vig doing karate moves, guys screaming and throwing toy footballs—it was chaotic, loud, and felt like we were all bonded in this intense moment of release.

grounded_facts: Two soldiers fire their fingers like pistols at Troy on the floor and scream like fierce animals, simulating a mock attack.
memories.memory_text: I remember being on the floor when two soldiers pointed their fingers at me like pistols and screamed like wild animals, as if they were launching a mock attack.

grounded_facts: Vig screams directly into Troy's face at point-blank range, mimicking animalistic or combat energy, which Troy immediately returns.
memories.memory_text: Vig screamed right in my face, so I screamed back just as loud—I matched his roar with my own, feeling that raw energy pass between us.

grounded_facts: Vig points a gun at surrendering Iraqis and demands to know if they committed atrocities in Kuwait.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig pull out his pistol and point it at the surrendering Iraqis, yelling at them and demanding to know if they'd committed atrocities in Kuwait, so I stepped in and pushed his gun away to keep things under control.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Officer refuses to disrobe when ordered, standing in contrast to others who comply.
memories.memory_text: I saw the older Iraqi officer refusing to take off his clothes when ordered, standing there while everyone else complied, and I heard Vig say he wouldn't obey the spirit of the order.

grounded_facts: After refusing to comply voluntarily, the Iraqi Officer is physically forced to remove his clothing by Vig and Walter.
memories.memory_text: I punched the Iraqi officer in the head when he still wouldn't move, and then I helped Vig and Walter forcibly pull his pants off.

grounded_facts: A group of Iraqi civilians and soldiers surrender in the desert and are subjected to disarming, disrobing, and inspection by U.S. troops.
memories.memory_text: I was there when a large group of Iraqi soldiers and civilians surrendered in the desert, and I saw them disarming, disrobing, and being inspected by our troops—I even had to punch an officer who refused to comply, and I noticed a document stuck in his backside, which I knew hadn't been swallowed because it was too clean, so I pulled out my latex glove to handle it.

grounded_facts: Troy instructs Vig to retrieve the document from the officer's body, then justifies the order through chain of command.
memories.memory_text: I told Vig to get the paper from the officer's body, and when he hesitated, I reminded him that we follow the chain of command—I had to make sure it was done.

grounded_facts: A rolled-up greasy paper is extracted from the Iraqi Officer's rectum and revealed to be a handwritten map with strategic markings.
memories.memory_text: I saw the greasy paper pulled from the officer's rectum, and when Vig unrolled it, I realized it was a handwritten map with markings that looked important.

grounded_facts: Cathy asks Archie to help her find a man named Barlow who may have information about the gold, based on a map allegedly retrieved from a prisoner's body.
memories.memory_text: I was told that someone named Barlow, maybe in Company B, might have information about the gold, based on a map that was supposedly retrieved from a prisoner's body.

grounded_facts: Archie uses infrared light to reveal a hidden map on the document, showing a different set of bunkers farther west.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie shine infrared light on the document, and right before my eyes, a hidden map appeared with green markings—showed a different set of bunkers farther west. We all stared at it in the glow, and Archie confirmed it was still three bunkers across three villages, just more to the west. I locked eyes with him, realizing this changed everything.

grounded_facts: Archie confronts Troy for control of the map, using psychological pressure and rank implication.
memories.memory_text: I remember Archie locking eyes with me, then reaching under the table to grab the map—I could see he was asserting control. We both held on for a moment, staring each other down, and when he asked to look at the map, his tone made it clear it wasn't a request. I let go, and we all watched together as the infrared light revealed the hidden markings.

grounded_facts: A meeting in the captain's tent where a hidden map is revealed and a gold heist plan is discussed.
memories.memory_text: I was in the captain's tent when Doc pulled out the document and opened it on the table with Vig and me. Archie pointed at each of us, and I picked up my family photo button. He demanded the map, and both of us held it, staring each other down. I told him we'd have to report to our commander if he took it. I said the map showed a series of bunkers near Karbala, and later questioned the risk of taking a Humvee, but Archie insisted the enemy was already beaten, deserting and surrendering all over. We all stared at the infrared-revealed map, and I saw the new set of bunkers farther west—realized this was serious, and that we could actually pull off this gold heist.

grounded_facts: Archie proposes a mission to steal Kuwaiti bullion from remote bunkers, framing it as a low-risk, high-reward operation.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Archie proposed stealing Kuwaiti bullion from remote bunkers, saying it would be easy with a beaten army and enough gold to get us out of our day jobs, and even though I questioned the risk of taking a Humvee, he convinced me it was low-risk.

grounded_facts: Archie formally takes control of the group, reassigning Walter and redirecting Bill Smithson's mission.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Archie took command and told us to salute him; I did as ordered and he even corrected my salute.

grounded_facts: Troy claims he threw the ball with a higher arc to make it easier for Doc to hit.
memories.memory_text: I threw the ball with a higher arc to make it easier for Doc to hit.

grounded_facts: Vig asserts that Black people make better receivers than quarterbacks, introducing racial stereotyping into the conversation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig say that Black people make better receivers than quarterbacks, and I knew right away this was going to stir things up.

grounded_facts: Doc cites Warren Moon as an excellent Black quarterback to challenge Vig's stereotype.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc respond to Vig by saying Warren Moon is an excellent quarterback, trying to push back against the stereotype.

grounded_facts: A discussion about Black quarterbacks in the NFL turns into a racially charged argument among the soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I remember the discussion turning into a heated argument about Black quarterbacks, so I told Doc not to get down in the mud with Vig and later said we could all agree there are many excellent Black quarterbacks to try to calm things down.

grounded_facts: The group starts a shooting game in the desert, using a football as a target for rifle and pistol fire.
A recreational shooting game conducted by soldiers during a Humvee journey across a war-damaged desert.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Humvee with Doc and Vig during our desert patrol, and we started a shooting game using a football as a target—Doc and I took turns throwing it and shooting at it with our rifle and pistol while it bounced across the sand.

grounded_facts: Archie forcefully silences the group after the argument becomes disruptive.
Archie abruptly stops the Humvee and silences the group after the argument escalates.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Humvee when Archie suddenly stopped the vehicle and shouted 'Shut the fuck up,' silencing everyone after the argument got out of hand.

grounded_facts: Troy kicks at the sand and uncovers a partially buried decayed human arm and body, revealing grim war remnants.
memories.memory_text: I kicked at the sand and uncovered a decayed human arm attached to a body, which shocked me.

grounded_facts: Vig questions Archie's statement about burying men alive, prompting Archie to clarify the military procedure and moral justification.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig question what Archie meant when he said they buried men alive, and then Archie explained the procedure.

grounded_facts: Archie Gates explains that U.S. forces used Bradleys with plows to bury Iraqi soldiers alive in trenches during the bombing campaign.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie Gates that U.S. forces used Bradleys with plows to bury Iraqi soldiers alive in trenches during the bombing campaign.

grounded_facts: Archie Gates leads a briefing in the desert to prepare the team for approaching the bunker using 'violence of action'.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie Gates that we would approach the bunker using 'violence of action,' and then we rehearsed the plan in the desert.

grounded_facts: The team arrives at the bunker site in a Humvee, preparing to engage with potential threats, encountering a booby-trapped cow.
memories.memory_text: I sat in the Humvee with the team, pistol ready, as we approached the bunker fast and stopped short near a cow we thought might be guarding the place.

grounded_facts: A cow near the bunker explodes when the Humvee approaches, splattering Troy and Doc with entrails.
memories.memory_text: I jumped out and flanked the cow with Doc when it suddenly exploded, splattering me with entrails, but I was unharmed.

grounded_facts: Troy quietly murmurs a plea for help from Rhonda, indicating anxiety or fear.
memories.memory_text: I quietly murmured a plea for help from Rhonda, feeling scared and overwhelmed in that moment.

grounded_facts: Archie asks Troy if he has seen any real combat action, probing his experience and reliability.
memories.memory_text: I was asked by Archie if I'd seen any real combat action, and I could tell he was questioning whether I could handle this situation.

grounded_facts: Archie takes Vig's big pistol and removes all shells, keeping them in his pocket.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie take Vig's big pistol and remove all the shells, putting them in his pocket, which made it clear he was taking control.

grounded_facts: Archie explains the physiological effects of gunshot wounds, including sepsis and tension pneumothorax, using a fantasy visualization of a bullet piercing tissue.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie explain how a bullet can cause sepsis, like a septic tank, with the lead tearing into the body, and he described tension pneumothorax as one of the worst wounds you can get.

grounded_facts: Troy asks if they can play Beach Boys music when entering the bunker, expressing a personal coping mechanism.
memories.memory_text: I asked if we could play the Beach Boys when we go in, because it calms me down—I'm not ashamed of liking them, and I think it helps more than Mozart would.

grounded_facts: A U.S. military team arrives at a village to locate and seize control of a bunker based on intelligence.
memories.memory_text: I inferred we had come to this village to find and take control of a bunker based on the map Archie was studying and the way he directed Vig toward that cement building with the soldiers in front.

grounded_facts: The Humvee arrives rapidly in the central square of a small village, creating tension among local inhabitants and soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Humvee as we sped into the village square, and I could see the fear in the locals and Iraqi soldiers as we zoomed past them and came to a sudden stop.

grounded_facts: Vig announces over a megaphone that they are U.S. Army and there to protect the locals.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig stand up and use the megaphone to tell the people we were U.S. Army and there to protect them, telling them to stay calm.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc disarm and detain two Iraqi soldiers guarding a cement building identified as the bunker.
memories.memory_text: I remember Doc and I jumping out of the Humvee with our pistols drawn, holding up our hands to stop the two Iraqi guards. We took their machine guns and made them lie face down on the ground, then I pulled out plastic twist cuffs to secure them.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi mother reveals her inability to feed her infant, appealing for milk.
memories.memory_text: I saw an Iraqi mother open her blouse and realized she couldn't feed her baby, then she said, 'No milk. Baby milk,' and I understood her desperation.

grounded_facts: Archie pushes Troy past the Iraqi mother who is asking for baby milk, refocusing him on the mission.
memories.memory_text: I was shocked by the mother's plea, but then Archie pushed me past her toward the bunker door, refocusing me on the mission.

grounded_facts: Archie begins running down the narrow stairs of the bunker, with Troy and Doc following behind.
memories.memory_text: I followed Archie and Doc as we ran down the narrow stairs into the bunker.

grounded_facts: Troy and Archie repeatedly kick and shoulder a locked door until it opens.
memories.memory_text: I shot the door lock and tried to shoulder it open, but it didn't budge until Archie and I kicked it together and finally got it open.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi soldier hugs Troy in apparent camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I was hugged by the Iraqi soldier, which felt awkward and made me uneasy despite his apparent friendliness.

grounded_facts: Doc restrains an Iraqi soldier by cuffing his hands behind his back.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc cuff the Iraqi soldier's hands behind his back and point his pistol at his face.

grounded_facts: Doc points his pistol and orders the Iraqi to let go of Troy.
memories.memory_text: I felt relief when Doc pointed his pistol at the Iraqi and ordered him to let go of me.

grounded_facts: A mission by Doc, Troy, and Archie to locate stolen gold in a bunker basement.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the mission with Doc and Archie to find the stolen gold in the bunker basement, not the chemical weapon.

grounded_facts: The Friendly Iraqi reveals that the gold has been moved from its expected location.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Iraqi say they had moved the gold, which meant our original plan was now useless.

grounded_facts: Archie and Doc open two crates and discover they are filled with hundreds of Kuwaiti passports instead of gold.
memories.memory_text: I helped Archie kick open the door and then we used power tools to open the crates, only to find they were filled with hundreds of Kuwaiti passports instead of the gold we were expecting.

grounded_facts: Archie, with support from Doc and Troy, pressures the Iraqi to reveal the gold's location using a map and gunpoint threat.
Doc, Troy, and Archie point guns at the Iraqi in a staged execution to extract information.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Doc and Archie as we pointed our guns and used the map to pressure the Iraqi, staging a threat to make him talk.

grounded_facts: The Friendly Iraqi offers to lead the group to the gold's location after being threatened.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi point to the map and offer to take us to the bunker where the gold was now hidden.

grounded_facts: A woman pleads for medical help for her injured child.
memories.memory_text: I saw a woman holding her shirtless son with a bandage around his chest, begging for hospital help.

grounded_facts: Doc pushes away a woman seeking medical help.
memories.memory_text: I watched Doc push the woman away from the Humvee when she was asking for medical help.

grounded_facts: A man grabs Archie while appealing for American help.
memories.memory_text: I saw a man grab Archie while shouting 'America help,' pleading for assistance.

grounded_facts: Troy forcibly removes a civilian who grabbed Archie.
memories.memory_text: I shoved the man off the vehicle when he grabbed Archie, forcing him away.

grounded_facts: Archie orders and Troy distributes MREs to the crowd.
memories.memory_text: Archie told me to give out MREs, so I ripped open the duffel and started handing them to the crowd.

grounded_facts: Archie forcibly removes Shiite civilians from the Humvee.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie shove the Shiite civilians out of the Humvee, and I looked back with him at the mess as we pulled away.

grounded_facts: An attack on a tanker truck results in chaos, milk spillage, and civilian response.
The driver of the tanker truck is killed during the attack.
memories.memory_text: I saw the tanker truck get hit and milk explode everywhere, spilling around our feet, and when Iraqi soldiers pulled the bodies from the cab, I knew the driver was dead.

grounded_facts: Archie shoves the friendly Iraqi out of the moving Hummer.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie shove the friendly Iraqi out of the moving Hummer, and I looked back with him as we pulled away.

grounded_facts: The tanker truck's container is exploded, releasing milk everywhere.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldier fire a grenade at the tanker truck, and then milk exploded everywhere, spilling around our feet and the Humvee before we pulled away.

grounded_facts: Archie takes off his gas suit in frustration and heat, revealing his sweat-drenched clothes underneath.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie rip off his gas suit, angry and soaked through his T-shirt.

grounded_facts: Following Archie's lead, the others remove their gas suits due to heat and exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I took off my gas suit too, just like the others, because we were all drenched and overheating.

grounded_facts: Vig fails to understand what a civil war is, prompting Troy to explain it.
memories.memory_text: I explained to Vig that a civil war is a war inside the same country when he didn't seem to understand what it meant.

grounded_facts: Archie hands out unmarked Marine uniforms to the group, signaling a shift in identity and plan.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie hand out Marine uniforms without name tags, and everyone else put them on.

grounded_facts: Archie repeatedly asks Troy what is most important in life, pushing him to reflect despite Troy's resistance.
memories.memory_text: Archie kept asking me what the most important thing in life was, pressing me even though I didn't want to engage in that kind of talk.

grounded_facts: Archie explains that 'necessity' governs actions, justifying their mission and the broader war logic.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie say that 'necessity' is what governs what happens in life, and that it justifies why we're still out here, taking risks even after the war's supposed to be over.

grounded_facts: Archie counters Troy's fear of being shot by arguing that locals are too afraid of them to attack.
memories.memory_text: I expressed my fear of being shot, and Archie told me the locals were too afraid of us to attack, saying they didn't touch us because we decimated their country.

grounded_facts: After discussion, the group agrees to proceed to another bunker to continue their mission.
memories.memory_text: After Archie suggested trying another bunker, I saw the others agree by saying 'Let's do it' and 'Rock and roll,' so I witnessed the group deciding to continue the mission.

grounded_facts: Troy refuses the uniform but puts on a kevlar vest, signaling conditional compliance.
memories.memory_text: I refused the Marine uniform but put on a kevlar vest from the Humvee because I needed some protection, even if the war was over.

grounded_facts: Troy refuses to put on the Marine uniform, expressing fear about personal risk and postwar consequences.
memories.memory_text: I refused to put on the Marine uniform because I've got a family, and I didn't want to risk getting shot after the war was already over—I pulled out my kevlar vest instead to stay protected.

grounded_facts: The Hummer arrives at the entrance of an underground bunker in a village piazza, marking the start of a military intervention.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Hummer racing into the village piazza and stopping right at the entrance of an underground bunker—we were there to make a move.

grounded_facts: Archie Gates uses a megaphone to declare U.S. military presence and order compliance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie Gates use the megaphone to declare we were the U.S. Marine Corps and order the soldiers to put their weapons down.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc forcibly disarm and detain two Iraqi soldiers who initially point rifles at them.
memories.memory_text: I helped Doc shove the two Iraqi soldiers face down in the dirt and cuff their hands behind their backs after they pointed rifles at us.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc verbally order the Iraqi soldiers to surrender their weapons.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at the Iraqi soldiers to drop their weapons, and then Doc and I forced them face down and cuffed them—I was part of taking them into custody.

grounded_facts: A U.S. military operation conducted in a village piazza to secure an underground bunker and neutralize local resistance.
memories.memory_text: I figured this was a full operation to secure the bunker and neutralize resistance in the piazza, given how we moved in with force and took control.

grounded_facts: Doc subdues and restrains an Iraqi soldier who had fled upon seeing the approaching team.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldier run when he spotted Archie, and then I ran past him with Archie while Doc came up behind and slammed him down, cuffing him right there.

grounded_facts: Archie kicks open a door and enters a room in the bunker, initiating the team's movement into a new space.
memories.memory_text: I followed Archie right after he kicked the door open and entered the bunker room.

grounded_facts: A U.S. military operation to secure an Iraqi bunker containing looted goods and personnel.
memories.memory_text: I burst into the bunker with Archie, guns drawn, to secure the place and take control of the situation.

grounded_facts: Archie declares the U.S. Marines' authority to confiscate Kuwaiti property under the cease-fire agreement.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie declare that the U.S. Marines had the authority to confiscate all Kuwaiti property stolen by Iraq under the cease-fire agreement.

grounded_facts: Doc strikes a resisting Iraqi with his pistol, causing it to fire accidentally, prompting everyone to duck.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc smack a resisting Iraqi with his pistol, and it went off accidentally, making everyone duck.

grounded_facts: Archie criticizes Doc for hitting a prisoner with his pistol after it discharges accidentally.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie tell Doc he shouldn't hit anyone with his pistol after it fired.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Captain offers Archie a Cuisinart for his wife, which Archie declines with a personal remark.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Captain offer Archie a Cuisinart for his wife, and I heard Archie refuse it by saying he's been divorced three times.

grounded_facts: Troy forces a kneeling Iraqi loading a CD to lie face down and cuffs him.
memories.memory_text: I pushed the man face down and cuffed his hands to secure him.

grounded_facts: Troy criticizes the Iraqi's music choice while forcing him to the ground.
memories.memory_text: I told the Iraqi that his music was bad and harmful while I had him on the ground.

grounded_facts: Doc punches a resisting Iraqi twice, causing him to cry.
memories.memory_text: I watched Doc punch the resisting Iraqi twice in the head, and the guy started crying.

grounded_facts: Troy identifies and points to a narrow door leading to another room, which Archie kicks open.
memories.memory_text: I spotted a narrow door in the corner and pointed it out, saying there was another room over there, and Archie immediately kicked it open.

grounded_facts: Archie backhands the Iraqi Sergeant and steps on his wrist to disarm him.
Archie physically assaults the Iraqi Sergeant and takes his pistol after pulling a cable from the water box.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie yank the cable out of the water box, then backhand the Iraqi Sergeant and step on his wrist to take his pistol.

grounded_facts: A scene in which Shiite captives are held in a water-filled box and others are bound and gagged while military personnel conduct or observe interrogation activities.
memories.memory_text: I saw a naked Shiite man in glasses sitting in a shallow box of water, shaking, and then noticed other Shiites—men, women, and children—bound and gagged across the room.

grounded_facts: Archie and the group arrive at Bunker Number Two after descending cement stairs, marking the start of a new phase in their mission.
memories.memory_text: I followed Archie and the others down a series of narrow cement stairs to reach Bunker Number Two, and I knew this was where our mission really began.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Captain expresses fear that Saddam will execute him over the situation.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Iraqi Captain say he was afraid Saddam would shoot him dead over the situation, and I could see the fear in his voice.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator responds by suggesting Saddam is more concerned about the Shiite than the gold.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Interrogator responding that Saddam worries more about the Shiite than the gold, shifting the focus away from the Captain's fear.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc disarm two guards outside a door in the basement, securing the immediate area.
memories.memory_text: I helped Doc disarm two guards outside the basement door, clearing the way for the team.

grounded_facts: Archie enters through the door, followed by the Iraqi Interrogator and Captain, advancing the group's position.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie go through the door, with the Iraqi Interrogator and Captain right behind him, moving the group forward.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Captain violently attacks Doc by jumping on his back and choking him, likely in response to the looting of the suitcases.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Captain suddenly jump on Doc's back and start choking him, and I reacted immediately by punching him in the head and pulling him off to stop the attack.

grounded_facts: Archie orders Doc and Troy to return the jewelry they stole from the suitcases, insisting they stick to the original plan of taking only gold.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie to put the jewelry back and stick to the plan—only gold.

grounded_facts: Archie uses verbal and physical dominance (pointing a gun) to assert control over the distribution of loot, ordering Doc and Troy to return stolen jewelry.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie point his gun and demand control, so I emptied my pockets along with Doc when he ordered us to return the jewelry.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Troy discover that multiple Louis Vuitton suitcases contain bricks of gold, each weighing five kilos, with sixty bricks per suitcase, leading to a total estimate of thirty million dollars.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Doc opened the suitcase and we all saw the gold bricks inside, each weighing five kilos, and I counted sixty in one suitcase; then we checked the others and found the same, realizing there was about thirty million dollars' worth.

grounded_facts: The suitcases, unable to bear the weight of the gold bricks, rip apart when lifted, causing gold to spill onto the floor and injure Troy.
memories.memory_text: I was lifting the suitcase with the gold when it suddenly ripped apart and a gold bar fell on my foot, causing me to jump in pain.

grounded_facts: A group of soldiers inspects a series of Louis Vuitton suitcases in a bunker and discovers they are filled with gold bricks, leading to shock, discussion, and attempts to move the loot.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Archie and Doc when we found the Louis Vuitton suitcases in the bunker, and I helped lay them out before we opened them; I saw the silverware, jewelry, and watches, and I even slipped some jewelry into my pocket until Archie made us return it; then when Doc opened one suitcase and froze, I cuffed the Iraqi Captain and looked over — and saw it was full of gold bricks; I picked one up and counted sixty in that case, and we found ten cases total, each with sixty bricks, and I remember Archie saying it was thirty million dollars; we tried lifting them sideways like tables because they were so heavy, but one ripped open and a gold bar landed on my foot, making me jump from the pain.

grounded_facts: Doc explains that the suitcases cannot support the weight of the gold due to insufficient tensile strength, based on his knowledge from working at an airport.
memories.memory_text: Doc told me the suitcases couldn't handle the weight of the gold because of insufficient tensile strength, something he knew from working at an airport, though I didn't fully understand what tensile strength meant at first.

grounded_facts: The group gathers in the bunker basement to pack gold bars into Louis Vuitton bags, discussing logistics and risks.
memories.memory_text: I was in the bunker basement with Doc, packing gold bars into Louis Vuitton bags while Archie paced nervously, and I could feel the tension in the air as we all realized how risky this was.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc pressure Archie to disclose how the gold will be shipped, showing distrust.
memories.memory_text: I looked Archie in the eye and told him he had to explain how the gold would be shipped, because Doc and I weren't going to move forward without knowing the plan.

grounded_facts: Archie explains the international smuggling route for the gold in response to Troy and Doc's insistence.
Archie reveals the full smuggling route for the gold, involving French Special Forces, oil barrels, and multiple international transfers.
memories.memory_text: I was told the full smuggling route when Archie finally broke under pressure: French Special Forces would hide the gold in oil barrels, drive it to Yanbu in Saudi, then ship it via Turkish boat to Perpignan, and from there on a French boat to Baltimore.

grounded_facts: Troy points out that the current containers won't fit in the Humvee, implying a flaw in the plan.
memories.memory_text: I told Archie these hat boxes ain't gonna fit in the Humvee, showing that our current plan has a flaw.

grounded_facts: The group decides they need a trailer to transport the gold bars because the hat boxes won't fit in the Humvee.
memories.memory_text: I pointed out that the hat boxes won't fit in the Humvee, which made the group realize we need a trailer; Archie then said we need a trailer, so I agreed to call U-Haul in Karbala to check availability.

grounded_facts: Troy moves upward through the bunker's narrow cement staircase.
memories.memory_text: I moved upward through the narrow cement staircase in the bunker, starting my way up the confined space.

grounded_facts: Vig asks Troy whether he successfully retrieved the object and if it is substantial.
Troy confirms that they have obtained an unspecified item, which is described as 'a lot'.
memories.memory_text: I remember Vig asking me if we got the item and whether it was a lot, and I confirmed to him that we got it and that it's a lot.

grounded_facts: Troy and Vig chain the ox cart to the Humvee, preparing for transport.
memories.memory_text: I worked with Vig to chain the ox cart to the Humvee so we could prepare for transport.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major warmly greets and embraces the Interrogator, signaling alliance or prior connection.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Major embrace the Interrogator warmly, which told me they had some kind of connection or alliance.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major salutes Archie, acknowledging his authority or role in the operation.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Iraqi Major saluting Archie right after the embrace, showing he recognized Archie's authority in the situation.

grounded_facts: Archie confirms with the Iraqi Major that they are taking the Kuwaiti gold, marking a commitment to the theft and collaboration with the Major.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie confirm directly to the Iraqi Major that we were taking the Kuwaiti gold, and the Major asked if we needed help with the load.

grounded_facts: A tense encounter outside Bunker Number Two where the protagonists meet the Iraqi Major amid ongoing violence against Shiites, negotiate the gold's transfer, and prepare to leave.
memories.memory_text: I was outside Bunker Number Two when we came out with the luggage, and I saw the Iraqi Major greet the Interrogator and salute Archie while violence was still happening around us, then they started talking about transferring the gold and whether we needed help loading.

grounded_facts: At the Iraqi Major's command, soldiers 6 & 7 are assigned to help load the luggage, indicating cooperation between the group and Iraqi forces.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Major call over soldiers 6 and 7 and assign them to help us load, even though Archie said we could do it ourselves.

grounded_facts: Archie notices blood on an Iraqi soldier's hands and face, leading to heightened awareness of recent violence.
memories.memory_text: I saw blood on one of the Iraqi soldier's hands and face, and I realized they'd just been involved in some brutal violence around here.

grounded_facts: After witnessing the violence and confirming the gold's acquisition, Archie orders the group to load up and depart.
memories.memory_text: I gave the order to load up and get out of there after seeing what happened and making sure we had the gold.

grounded_facts: After the cart fails, the group decides to load supplies into a truck instead.
memories.memory_text: After the cart collapsed, I said we should take the truck to carry the supplies instead.

grounded_facts: Archie challenges the Iraqi Major's actions using the Geneva Convention as moral leverage.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie challenges the Iraqi Major's actions using the Geneva Convention as moral leverage.

grounded_facts: Troy reminds Archie that their mission is about gold, not saving people.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Troy reminds Archie that their mission is about gold, not saving people.

grounded_facts: Archie offers gold in exchange for allowing Shiite prisoners to leave with them.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie offers gold in exchange for allowing Shiite prisoners to leave with them.

grounded_facts: Iraqi Major rejects Archie's offer of gold to free Shiite prisoners, citing fear of Saddam's retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Iraqi Major refuse Archie's offer of gold to free the Shiite prisoners, shouting that Saddam would kill him if they were let go.

grounded_facts: Archie instructs Troy and others to provide armed cover during his intervention.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie instructs Troy and others to provide armed cover during his intervention.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi soldier attacks the Man in Glasses and the Girl; Archie intervenes, disarms the soldier, and rescues them.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie walk right into it when the soldier attacked the man and the girl—he disarmed him, put him in a choke hold, and got them both to safety.

grounded_facts: Archie orders his team to cover him as he confronts Iraqi soldiers, leading to mutual gunpoint.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie orders his team to cover him as he confronts Iraqi soldiers, leading to mutual gunpoint.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers seize and execute a raped Shiite woman in front of the Americans.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldiers pull a woman from the group and shoot her dead right in front of us, and I had to look away—it shook me hard.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers hold Shiite prisoners, including a woman and a man with a girl, under armed guard near bunker two.
memories.memory_text: I saw Iraqi soldiers holding Shiite prisoners at gunpoint near bunker two, including a woman and a man with a girl, and I watched as they were roughed up and kept down by force.

grounded_facts: Iraqi 6 shoots Archie; Troy kills Iraqi 6; Iraqi 7 shoots Troy; Doc and Vig return fire, killing Iraqi 7 and two others; Archie kills Iraqi Major.
memories.memory_text: I saw Iraqi 6 shoot Archie, so I fired and killed him; then Iraqi 7 shot me, but I kept fighting while Doc and Vig returned fire and took him and two others down, and Archie executed the Iraqi Major.

grounded_facts: Troy is shot in the chest but survives due to kevlar; bullet falls out of vest dent.
memories.memory_text: I was hit in the chest and felt a sharp pain, but when I checked my vest afterward, the bullet had been stopped by the kevlar and fell out of the dent into my hand.

grounded_facts: After the firefight, surviving Iraqi soldiers drop weapons and surrender.
memories.memory_text: After the shooting stopped, I saw the remaining Iraqi soldiers drop their weapons and surrender, with one of them walking toward us with his hands up.

grounded_facts: Troy challenges Archie's decision to evacuate prisoners, citing mission necessity and personal risk.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Troy challenges Archie's decision to evacuate prisoners, citing mission necessity and personal risk.

grounded_facts: Archie forcefully orders Troy to obey and make room for the prisoners.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie forcefully orders Troy to obey and make room for the prisoners.

grounded_facts: Doc questions Troy's lack of empathy by asking him to imagine being a prisoner.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Doc questions Troy's lack of empathy by asking him to imagine being a prisoner.

grounded_facts: Doc challenges Troy by asking him to imagine being in the prisoners' position.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Doc challenges Troy by asking him to imagine being in the prisoners' position.

grounded_facts: Troy displays his Kevlar vest with a bullet impact to argue against risking lives for others.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Troy displays his Kevlar vest with a bullet impact to argue against risking lives for others.

grounded_facts: Archie insists that space be made in the vehicles for the Shiite prisoners despite resistance from Troy.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie insists that space be made in the vehicles for the Shiite prisoners despite resistance from Troy.

grounded_facts: The team starts vehicles and begins evacuation with prisoners.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The team starts vehicles and begins evacuation with prisoners.

grounded_facts: An approaching Iraqi tank is unable to engage as its turret becomes stuck, halting immediate threat.
memories.memory_text: I remember that An approaching Iraqi tank is unable to engage as its turret becomes stuck, halting immediate threat.

grounded_facts: Troy drives the truck at maximum speed, falling 60 yards behind the Humvee while expressing frustration.
memories.memory_text: I pushed the truck as fast as it would go, bouncing hard on the road while falling behind the Humvee, and I could feel my frustration building.

grounded_facts: The tank is turning into position to target the Humvee, observed through Doc's binoculars.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc say the tank was lining us up, so I figured it was turning into position to target the Humvee, but I wasn't entirely sure what they could see through the binoculars.

grounded_facts: A rocket explodes in the sky above the Humvee, releasing a brown gas cloud.
Doc announces that the cloud from the explosion is gas, providing critical information.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the Humvee when I saw a rocket streak across the sky and explode into a brown gas cloud above us, and then I heard Doc shout 'Gas.'

grounded_facts: A group travels by Humvee across the desert during daylight when an aerial attack and subsequent mine explosion disrupt the journey.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a group traveling by Humvee across the desert in daylight when the rocket attack happened, followed by a mine explosion that disrupted our journey.

grounded_facts: The truck driven by Troy crashes after flying debris smashes the windshield, causing Troy to jerk the wheel and flip the vehicle onto its side, sliding across the sand.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the truck when flying debris smashed the windshield, and I instinctively jerked the wheel, causing the truck to flip onto its side and slide across the sand.

grounded_facts: Troy shouts at the children running across the minefield to stop, but they do not heed him.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at the children to stop, but they kept running and didn't listen to me.

grounded_facts: Troy sees two children running across the minefield and chases after them despite the danger.
memories.memory_text: I saw two children running across the minefield, screaming, and I ran after them as fast as I could, the hat cases banging against my legs.

grounded_facts: Archie stops Doc from injecting himself with a syringe, correctly identifying the gas as non-lethal C.S.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie grab Doc's hand just as he was about to inject himself, and I heard Archie say, 'Don't do it, this isn't sarin. We'd be dead by now.'

grounded_facts: Archie identifies the brown fog as C.S. gas, not sarin or mustard gas, and explains it is non-lethal but extremely irritating.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie say the brown fog was tear gas times ten, explaining it was C.S. gas—non-lethal but extremely irritating.

grounded_facts: Troy catches up to the Girl and scoops her up, covering her face with her coat to protect her during the chase through the minefield.
memories.memory_text: I chased the children through the brown fog, dropped one suitcase, and scooped up the girl with my left arm, covering her face with her coat to protect her.

grounded_facts: Troy drops the second suitcase and grabs the Boy, carrying both children under his arms as he runs.
memories.memory_text: I dropped my other suitcase, caught the boy, and had both kids under my arms like footballs before someone grabbed me from behind.

memories.memory_text: I was suddenly grabbed from behind with a cord around my neck and knocked down, unable to move as I landed on my back with the children still in my arms.

memories.memory_text: I was running through a minefield after the boy, trying to get both children to safety, but I wasn't sure if I could make it before being caught.

memories.memory_text: I was downed and they tore the screaming children from my arms.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Interrogator, wearing a gas mask, kick me in the head as I was lying on the ground.

grounded_facts: As Troy reaches for his pistol, Iraqi soldiers rip it from his hand and drag him away.

memories.memory_text: I reached for my pistol, but the Iraqi soldiers ripped it from my hand as they dragged me away.

grounded_facts: Doc tells Vig he will die if he doesn't comply, attempting to coerce him into the tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc tell Vig he was going to die if he didn't go into the tunnel, trying to force him back.

memories.memory_text: I inferred that Vig and Doc started fighting after Doc kept pushing to get into the tunnel.

memories.memory_text: I saw Vig jerk his arm away and punch Doc when he was grabbed.

grounded_facts: Archie calls out and searches for Barlow in the haze.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Archie called out for me while searching in the haze.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers remove Troy's clothes, leaving him naked during captivity.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Iraqi soldiers stripping me, leaving me naked in the desert ruins.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi soldier asks if they can execute Troy, indicating uncertainty about handling American prisoners.
memories.memory_text: I heard one of the soldiers ask if they could shoot me, like they weren't even sure what to do with an American prisoner.

grounded_facts: The interrogator asserts that Troy's presence proves the Americans violated the ceasefire.
memories.memory_text: I was told I was proof that the Americans broke the ceasefire, that my presence meant they'd violated the agreement.

grounded_facts: Amid the chaos of the firefight, Troy tries to flee but is caught and dragged toward the bunker.
memories.memory_text: I tried to run during the chaos, but I was tackled and dragged back toward the bunker while naked.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi interrogator confronts Troy while soldiers debate his status as a prisoner.
memories.memory_text: I saw the interrogator pull off his mask and confront me while the soldiers argued around us, and when the shooting started, I tried to run but was tackled and dragged toward the bunker.

grounded_facts: Troy is being led naked through a narrow corridor in the bunker by two soldiers, indicating a loss of autonomy and possible vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I was naked and being led down a narrow corridor by two soldiers, and I could feel my complete lack of control over what was happening to me.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi soldier gives a blunt order for Troy to get dressed, showing authority and disregard.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Iraqi soldier bark the same order twice—'Get dress'—showing no respect, just raw authority.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi soldier throws Troy and his clothes into a bathroom and orders him to get dressed before slamming the door, initiating his confinement.
memories.memory_text: I was thrown into a bathroom with my clothes, and an Iraqi soldier ordered me to get dressed before slamming the door behind me.

grounded_facts: Troy is held in a crude cement bathroom filled with looted consumer goods, where he attempts to use stolen cell phones to call for help.
memories.memory_text: I found myself in a crude cement room filled with looted goods, and I kicked through the stuff, trying to use stolen cell phones to call for help while blocking the door with debris.

grounded_facts: Troy reaches a phone operator with a British accent and tries to explain an emergency, asking for 'Operation Desert Storm', but fails when the line dies.
memories.memory_text: I reached an operator with a British accent and tried to explain there was an emergency, but I couldn't get through clearly; I said 'Operation Desert Storm' hoping that would help them understand the urgency, and when I heard nothing, I said 'hello?' before the line went dead.

grounded_facts: After being thrown into a crude bathroom filled with looted items, Troy discovers a pile of cell phones and repeatedly tries to use them to make an emergency call, eventually reaching an operator but failing to get assistance before the line dies.
memories.memory_text: I was thrown into a bathroom full of looted stuff and found a bunch of cell phones; I kept trying them one after another, desperate to make an emergency call, and when one finally worked and then died, I threw it down and started searching through more, muttering 'come on' to myself as I tried to get a dial tone again.

grounded_facts: Darlene shares her emotional and physical exhaustion due to caring for the baby alone and missing Troy.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Darlene that she's been really tired and lonely, taking care of the baby without help, and that she misses me a lot.

grounded_facts: Troy informs Darlene that he is trapped in a bunker near 223 north outside Karbala, indicating ongoing danger despite the declared end of the war.
memories.memory_text: I told Darlene I'm stuck in a bunker near 223 north outside Karbala, hoping she'd understand how bad it is even though the war was supposed to be over.

grounded_facts: Troy asks Darlene to tell Krystal he is a rich man and that she will be taken care of, implying financial or emotional provision.
memories.memory_text: I asked Darlene to tell Krystal I'm a rich man and that she'll be taken care of, no matter what happens.

grounded_facts: Troy tells Darlene he loves her amid escalating danger, reinforcing their emotional bond.
memories.memory_text: I told Darlene I love her, right before I had to go—she needed to hear it one more time.

grounded_facts: A tense phone conversation between Troy and Darlene, during which Troy reveals he is trapped in a bunker and under attack, ending with his capture.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone with Darlene, telling her I love her and that Krystal will be taken care of, but then another mortar hit the bunker—dust everywhere—and I could hear her fear; I tried to finish, to say everything, but the soldiers burst in, punched me, and dragged me away before I could say goodbye.

grounded_facts: Soldiers break into the bunker, physically assault Troy, and drag him away during the phone call.
memories.memory_text: I was on the phone when soldiers broke through the door, punched me in the face, and dragged me away.

grounded_facts: Voltage is applied through a wire wrapped around Troy's head, causing physical pain and dental damage, marking a key escalation in interrogation tactics.
memories.memory_text: I felt the voltage surge through the wire wrapped around my head, making my teeth clench so hard they chipped, and I could taste blood from my nose and lip as I fought not to cry.

grounded_facts: The interrogator links Michael Jackson's alleged pedophilia to American moral decay, accusing Troy of representing a country that disrespects children.
memories.memory_text: I was told that my country is sick and disrespects children, and that Michael Jackson turning his skin white was because America made him hate himself, just like we hate Arabs and bomb children here.

grounded_facts: A formal but brutal interrogation of Troy by Iraqi soldiers in a bunker, combining physical torture, psychological pressure, and personal revelation.
memories.memory_text: I was interrogated in a bunker where they asked me about my rank and whether our army helped Shiite children, and when I didn't give the answer they wanted, they shocked me through the wire on my head.

grounded_facts: The interrogator reveals that his one-year-old son was killed in a bombing while asleep in bed, marking a shift from aggression to personal grief.
memories.memory_text: I heard the interrogator tell me about his son who was killed in a bombing while asleep, and I could hear the pain in his voice when he spoke.

grounded_facts: Troy reveals he has a daughter to establish common ground with the interrogator after learning of his son's death.
Troy discloses his newborn daughter's name, Krystal, during interrogation, establishing a personal connection with the interrogator.
memories.memory_text: I told him I have a daughter too, and I said her name is Krystal because I wanted him to see me as a father like him.

grounded_facts: Vig reaches out to Doc as a gesture of apology and connection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig reach out to Doc, trying to make things right between them.

grounded_facts: Troy argues that the art of war should aim to preserve life through strategy, not cause unnecessary death.
memories.memory_text: I told the Interrogator that the art of war isn't about killing people—it's a strategy to preserve life with as little violence as possible.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator challenges Troy on the moral emptiness of their roles, using his son's death to accuse Troy of personal responsibility.
memories.memory_text: I was told the Interrogator joined Saddam's army to provide for his family, and he challenged me by saying our jobs were the same when he asked how I'd feel if his bomb killed my daughter, blaming me for his son's death.

grounded_facts: A structured session in which the Interrogator questions and confronts Troy, blending personal history, moral argument, and physical violence.
memories.memory_text: I was in a harsh interrogation where the Interrogator questioned me, confronted me about my role, and eventually broke my nose with repeated blows while I tried to hold my ground.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator repeatedly strikes Troy's nose with a golf club, ultimately breaking it to convey his emotional pain.
memories.memory_text: I felt the Interrogator strike my nose repeatedly with a golf club, and I remember the crack when he finally broke it, using the pain to show me his grief.

grounded_facts: Troy implies that the Interrogator's son's death was a consequence of Saddam's invasion of Kuwait, linking geopolitical events to personal loss.
memories.memory_text: I told the Interrogator that his son wouldn't be dead if Saddam hadn't invaded Kuwait, linking his loss to the war's origins.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator questions Troy's sincerity and reduces his stated moral cause to materialism, asking if he fights for a pickup truck.
memories.memory_text: I was asked if I was fighting for a pickup truck, and I knew they were trying to reduce my reasons to something materialistic, which wasn't true.

grounded_facts: Troy argues that while excessive bombing is wrong, failing to save Kuwait undermines global stability.
memories.memory_text: I argued that while too much bombing is crazy, not saving Kuwait undermines stability, and I emphasized that we need to stabilize the region.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator uses a CD pulled from Troy's pocket as a funnel to pour crude oil from a bucket into Troy's mouth, symbolically punishing Troy for Western intervention.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Interrogator pulling a CD from my pocket and forcing it into my mouth, then using it to pour crude oil from a bucket into me—he did it like a punishment for what the West has done in Iraq.

grounded_facts: A coercive questioning session in which Troy is physically and psychologically pressured by the Interrogator and a second Iraqi.
memories.memory_text: I was in a room where the Interrogator and another Iraqi pressured me, stuffing a CD into my mouth and forcing crude oil down my throat while I could do nothing to stop it.

grounded_facts: Archie shoots and kills two Iraqi guards in the control room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie kick in the door and shoot two Iraqi guards who were trying to fix the emergency light in the control room.

grounded_facts: Archie shoots the Interrogator in the thigh during confrontation.
Archie shoots the Interrogator in the thigh to incapacitate him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie shoot the Interrogator in the thigh, and I felt blood spatter on my face as he went down.

grounded_facts: Archie disconnects Troy from the interrogation equipment and cuts him loose from the chair.
memories.memory_text: I felt Archie rip the wires off me and cut the cord binding me to the chair, freeing me from the restraints.

grounded_facts: Archie locates and rescues Troy from captivity in the bunker's control room after eliminating enemy personnel.
memories.memory_text: Archie found me in the control room, ripped the wires from my jaw, cut the cords binding me to the chair, and gave me a pistol after freeing me from captivity.

grounded_facts: Archie gives Troy a pistol after freeing him.
Archie hands his newly acquired pistol to Troy after freeing him.
memories.memory_text: I remember Archie taking the Interrogator's pistol and handing it to me after he cut me loose.

grounded_facts: Troy points a pistol directly at the Interrogator's face to assert dominance.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my pistol right into the Interrogator's face, staring him down to show I was in control now.

grounded_facts: Troy chooses not to kill the wounded Interrogator, firing beside his head instead.
Troy points a gun at the Interrogator but chooses not to kill him, firing beside his head instead.
memories.memory_text: I fired my gun beside his head instead of killing him, because I didn't want to become that person, even though I had the chance.

grounded_facts: Doc shoots the lock on the inner door, allowing it to open.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Doc must have shot the lock on the inner door because it suddenly opened after the gunfire.

grounded_facts: Archie rushes by with Troy and calls out to move forward.
memories.memory_text: I was with Archie when he rushed past me and shouted 'Come on,' so I moved forward with him.

grounded_facts: Archie and Troy leave the bunker.
memories.memory_text: I ran out of the bunker with Archie.

grounded_facts: Archie and Troy retreat into the bunker after the grenade explosion.
A grenade fired from the helicopter explodes next to Archie and Troy, forcing them to retreat.
memories.memory_text: I was right there with Archie when the helicopter fired a grenade that exploded next to us, and I immediately scrambled back into the bunker to get to safety.

grounded_facts: Archie and Troy arrive at the bunker door and knock Doc over upon encountering him.
memories.memory_text: I ran into Doc at the bunker door with Archie and knocked him over when we got there.

grounded_facts: Archie and Troy crouch inside the door for cover or protection after entering.
memories.memory_text: I crouched down inside the door with Archie right after we entered, trying to stay out of sight from the chopper hovering outside.

grounded_facts: Archie gives the C-4 football bomb to Doc, assigning him the role of deploying the explosive.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie hand the C-4 football bomb to Doc, assigning him to deploy it during our escape.

grounded_facts: Archie pretends to throw the football bomb to illustrate the correct timing and motion for deployment.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie pretend to throw the football bomb, using the motion to show the right timing and form we'd need for the real throw.

Archie directs the group on an escape procedure, distributing tasks and demonstrating the timing for throwing a C-4 football bomb.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie to follow his instructions exactly, and he directed us on how to escape, including the timing for throwing the football bomb, saying 'Step, throw, one-two -- I'm gonna give it a five second fuse. That gives you two steps out the door.'

grounded_facts: Archie cuts the fuse on the football-shaped C-4 explosive, preparing it for use.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie cut the fuse on the football-shaped C-4 with his knife, getting it ready for use while I held the lighter.

grounded_facts: A coordinated effort by Archie, Doc, and Troy to flee the bunker using an explosive device, following Archie's instructions.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the coordinated effort with Archie and Doc to flee the bunker, standing ready at the door with my lighter as we prepared to execute the escape together.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie physically stabilizes Troy's shaking hand to help him light the fuse, showing teamwork and composure under pressure.

grounded_facts: The fuse is successfully ignited with Archie's help after Troy struggles to light it due to shaking hands.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The fuse is successfully ignited with Archie's help after Troy struggles to light it due to shaking hands.

memories.memory_text: I was told that After the fuse is lit, Archie instructs Troy to leave immediately, signaling urgency and transition to the next phase of their plan.

grounded_facts: Archie and Troy exit the bunker while firing pistols, beginning their escape under fire.
memories.memory_text: I fired my pistol as Archie and I rushed out of the bunker, starting our escape under fire.

grounded_facts: Doc throws a burning fuse ball toward the hovering chopper in an attempt to damage it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc throw a burning fuse ball at the hovering chopper, trying to take it down.

grounded_facts: Troy ignites the second fuse, initiating an explosive sequence.
memories.memory_text: I lit the second fuse, knowing it would set off the explosion we needed.
