memories.memory_text: I remember rushing out of the bunker with Archie, both of us firing our pistols, while Doc ran in the middle carrying the ball.

grounded_facts: Doc throws a football that hits the chopper, causing it to explode and crash.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc throw that football, and I couldn't believe it when it hit the chopper and made it explode—I watched the whole thing crash down right in front of us.

grounded_facts: Archie knocks down a rising Iraqi soldier and disarms him; Doc binds him with a plastic cuff.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie knock down an Iraqi soldier who tried to rise, and then Doc moved in and cuffed him with a plastic tie—I was right there watching it go down.

grounded_facts: After confirming Imam's identity, Troy embraces him in relief.
memories.memory_text: When I confirmed it was Imam, I hugged him tight and asked how his girl was—I felt a real sense of relief seeing him alive.

grounded_facts: Troy declares intent to help the Shiite refugees despite logistical challenges.
memories.memory_text: I told Doc I knew what I was saying—we weren't just stealing supplies, we were going to help these Shiite refugees, no matter how hard it seemed.

grounded_facts: The group secures the area after the chopper explosion, disarms enemy soldiers, and processes prisoners.
memories.memory_text: After the crash, I helped secure the area—we took weapons from the wounded, Archie and Doc disarmed a soldier who tried to get up, and then we made sure the battlefield was under control.

grounded_facts: Archie directs Doc and others to secure the perimeter after Vig is shot.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie shout 'Cover him' and then 'Lock it down. Shoot anything that moves' while Doc and the others scrambled to secure the perimeter.

grounded_facts: Vig is shot in the collarbone while running toward the group, continues moving briefly before collapsing.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig get hit in the collarbone and stumble, but he kept moving toward me, so I ran as hard as I could to reach him and caught him in my arms just as he collapsed.

grounded_facts: Troy is hit by a gunshot in the lower right chest, sustaining a penetrating wound and falling beside Vig.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sudden impact in my lower right chest, the force spinning me around before I fell beside Vig, both of us on the ground, looking at each other.

grounded_facts: Vig reunites with the group but is shot shortly after; Troy is also shot during the same exchange.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig come toward me, blood on his mouth, and I caught him when he fell—I hugged him, and then I got hit too, spinning around from the shot before collapsing beside him.

grounded_facts: Troy is inside his own rib cage, struggling to breathe as others attend to him.
memories.memory_text: I could feel my breaths straining, crushing my organs to the left, and I saw Doc leaning over me, speaking but I couldn't hear anything over my own labored breathing.

grounded_facts: Vig is no longer breathing, indicating death or unconsciousness.
memories.memory_text: I turned my gaze to the side and saw Vig—no movement, no breath—just stillness, and I realized he wasn't breathing anymore.

grounded_facts: Archie opens his waist pack and takes out a sterile scalpel, suggesting medical or surgical intent.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie open his waist pack and take out a sterile scalpel, like he was about to do some kind of medical procedure on me.

grounded_facts: Imam's Little Girl gets out of the passenger side of the Jaguar and approaches the scene despite being scolded.
Imam scolds his daughter and gestures for her to return to safety.
Imam's Little Girl hugs Imam while staring down at Troy, showing emotional engagement with the situation.
While embracing her father, the Little Girl looks down at Troy with apparent recognition or concern.
memories.memory_text: I saw Imam's Little Girl get out of the Jaguar despite him scolding her and gesturing for her to go back, and then she hugged him while staring down at me with a look of recognition or concern.

grounded_facts: An urgent medical intervention takes place in the desert after Troy is shot and develops breathing complications.
memories.memory_text: I was shot and couldn't breathe, lying there in the desert while Archie and Doc worked on me to save my life.

grounded_facts: Archie performs a needle decompression on Troy's chest to release trapped air, relieving his breathing difficulty.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie plunge the scalpel into my chest and felt the huge relief when the air rushed out and I could finally breathe again.

grounded_facts: Archie inserts an IV tube into the decompression site to maintain air release and possibly prepare for further treatment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie insert an IV tube into the hole in my chest to keep the air from building up again and maybe to give me treatment.

grounded_facts: The last Iraqi gunner is shot and killed by five Shiite rifle men in the desert.
memories.memory_text: I saw the five Shiite rifle men chase down and shoot the last Iraqi gunner in the desert.

grounded_facts: Troy sits up and watches the aftermath of the shooting.
memories.memory_text: I sat up and watched the aftermath of the shooting.

grounded_facts: A spontaneous mourning ritual around Vig's body in the trunk of the Jaguar, involving prayer and chant by Shiite women and children, observed by Archie, Troy, and Doc.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Shiite women and children praying and chanting around Vig's body in the trunk of the Jaguar.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc silently reenact Vig's signature Karate arm dance as a tribute to him.
memories.memory_text: I joined Doc in doing a quiet version of Vig's Karate arm dance as our own way of honoring him.

grounded_facts: Archie removes Vig's pistol from his clenched hand, symbolizing the transfer of responsibility and legacy.
memories.memory_text: I watched Archie take Vig's pistol from his hand, a solemn moment that felt like a passing of duty.

grounded_facts: Archie declares that the group is now Vig's family and takes responsibility for his remains, marking a shift in group identity and duty.
memories.memory_text: I heard Archie say we were now Vig's family and that he'd take responsibility for his remains.

grounded_facts: Archie gently removes Vig's glasses, a quiet act of respect and closure.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie gently remove Vig's glasses, a quiet gesture that brought a sense of closure.

grounded_facts: The group agrees to take Vig's body to the shrine at Kajatar in Iran, enacting his final wish.
memories.memory_text: I learned we agreed to take Vig's body to the shrine at Kajatar in Iran, fulfilling his final wish.

grounded_facts: A temporary stop in the desert where the group manages injuries and secures loot.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in a folding chair in the desert, hurting and trying to manage my injuries while the group took a temporary stop to secure the loot.

grounded_facts: Archie fills a rusted oil drum with gold bars and seals it with tape.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie fill a rusted oil drum with gold bars and tape it shut while I sat nearby, feeling pained and uncomfortable.

grounded_facts: Archie explains to Troy that he must release the chest tube valve every fifteen minutes to prevent pressure buildup.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie that I need to release the chest tube valve every fifteen minutes to prevent pressure from building up.

grounded_facts: Archie releases built-up air pressure from the tube in Troy's chest, providing temporary relief.
memories.memory_text: I felt relief when Archie released the built-up air from the tube in my chest.

grounded_facts: Archie estimates Troy can survive approximately four hours if internal bleeding does not worsen.
memories.memory_text: I was told I might have about four hours left if I'm not bleeding too badly inside.

grounded_facts: Troy states he is very thirsty, indicating physical distress.
memories.memory_text: I said I'm really thirsty because I'm in physical distress.

grounded_facts: DOC informs Troy that there is no available water.
memories.memory_text: I was told there's no water available, so I can't drink anything.

grounded_facts: Archie hands over an urn of filtered water to thirsty members of the group, demonstrating care and cooperation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie hand an urn of filtered water to the thirsty group, and I noticed how they drank it right away.

grounded_facts: The group begins extracting water from snow globes by cracking them open and filtering the liquid, turning a symbolic object into a survival resource.
memories.memory_text: I cracked open a snow globe and filtered the water with a Shiite, and later I did the same with Doc, turning those little ornaments into something we could actually drink.

grounded_facts: Archie, Troy, and Doc distribute filtered water to dehydrated members of the group, alleviating immediate physical need.
memories.memory_text: I helped distribute filtered water to the dehydrated people, passing it out with Doc to meet their urgent need.

grounded_facts: The Vuitton suitcases are set on fire with gasoline and a match, resulting in their destruction.
memories.memory_text: I threw a match onto the pile of Vuitton suitcases after Imam poured gasoline on them, and I saw them burst into flames right away.

grounded_facts: Imam distributes gold bars to Shiite peasants, who conceal them and prepare to leave.
memories.memory_text: I watched Imam hand out gold bars to the Shiite peasants while I waited with Archie and Doc, and I saw them stash the gold in their clothes and bags before we all kept waiting together.

grounded_facts: Troy and Walter exchange a fist bump and banter about their mission.
memories.memory_text: I fist-bumped Walter and told him I was protecting the free peoples of the world, and he joked about getting me fixed up to go home.

grounded_facts: A gathering at the desert bunker where medical aid is given, gold is accounted for, and the group prepares for transport.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp pain and then released the valve on my chest tube, hearing the hiss of air and feeling relief, while we all sat waiting for the evacuation, and later I got an IV from Walter.

grounded_facts: Walter and Doc administer penicillin via IV to Troy and Archie.
memories.memory_text: I felt Walter push an IV needle into my arm while Doc did the same for Archie, giving us penicillin to help us recover.

grounded_facts: A U.S. military convoy arrives at the bunker to extract the group.
memories.memory_text: I heard the rumble of motors approaching and saw a U.S. military convoy arrive with trucks and a Humvee, and I knew we were being extracted—I sat in the back of a crowded truck with Imam and his daughter, smiling as we prepared to go home.

grounded_facts: The organized departure of the group in a military convoy toward the Iranian border.
memories.memory_text: I saw the convoy approaching in the desert and we all watched it come in, then I got into the back of a crowded truck with Imam and his daughter, smiling as we rolled out toward the border behind the Humvee.

grounded_facts: The convoy departs the bunker with Shiites, Imam, his daughter, and the team heading toward the Iranian border.
memories.memory_text: I watched the convoy approach and then helped load the Shiites, Imam, his daughter, and the gold onto the trucks before we all climbed in; I remember sitting in the back of a crowded truck with them as we rolled out toward the Iranian border.

grounded_facts: Archie decides the group will escort the refugees on foot to the Iranian side and return.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Archie that we'd be walking the refugees to the Iranian border and then returning to the trucks.

grounded_facts: Doc turns and signals the drivers to move forward.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc turn and signal the drivers to move forward.

grounded_facts: Troy and the U.S. drivers disengage safeties on their rifles in preparation for movement.
memories.memory_text: I took the safety off my M-16 and saw the other U.S. drivers doing the same as we got ready to move out on foot.

grounded_facts: An organized movement of Shiite refugees and U.S. soldiers through a narrow opening in razor wire at an international border.
The group of Shiites, carrying Vig's body and flanked by U.S. soldiers, crosses the border through a narrow opening in the razor wire.
memories.memory_text: I helped lead the group of Shiites through a narrow opening in the razor wire, carrying Vig's body, with me and the other U.S. soldiers flanking them to keep everyone safe as we crossed the border.

grounded_facts: Doc responds to Troy's sudden dizziness by telling him to stay back, showing concern for his condition.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc tell me to stay back when I started feeling dizzy, so I knew he was concerned about me.

grounded_facts: Troy suddenly drops to one knee and reports feeling dizzy, prompting concern from Doc.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly dropped to one knee and told Doc I was just dizzy or something, though I didn't know what caused it — I knew it wasn't the air.

grounded_facts: Captain Van Meter verbally attacks Troy during his arrest, refusing to help him breathe.
memories.memory_text: I heard Captain Van Meter shout down at me, telling me to shut my goddamn mouth when I couldn't breathe, after he refused to help me.

grounded_facts: Archie pleads with General Horn to provide medical attention to Troy, who is suffocating due to his restraints.
memories.memory_text: I saw Archie drag the MP toward General Horn and plead with him not to let me die, begging for medical help while I was on the ground.

grounded_facts: Troy, handcuffed behind his back, cannot access his breathing valve and begins to suffocate; a soldier cuts his cuffs, allowing him to breathe.
memories.memory_text: I was cuffed behind my back and couldn't reach my breathing valve—I started suffocating until a soldier cut my cuffs and I could finally turn the valve and breathe again.

grounded_facts: Archie reveals the gold and appeals to General Horn's sense of honor and ambition to save the Shiites.
Archie reveals the presence of stolen Kuwaiti gold to General Horn, who verifies it and shifts his stance on the situation.
memories.memory_text: I was held in custody with Doc when Archie revealed we had the Kuwaiti gold, and I saw the MP spill the bars onto the sand; I watched General Horn examine it and saw how his attitude changed after Archie appealed to his honor.

grounded_facts: General Horn orders the confiscation of news cameras and tapes, suppressing media coverage of the event.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Horn shove a news camera to the ground and order the MPs to take the tapes, shutting down all the media coverage right there.

grounded_facts: Archie, Troy, and Doc are formally arrested and ordered to disclose the location of the bullion before being taken away.
memories.memory_text: I was told by General Horn that I was under arrest, facing a court-martial, and ordered to reveal where the bullion was before being taken away.

grounded_facts: Six Apache helicopters arrive and land between Archie and the border, blocking the path and initiating U.S. military intervention.
memories.memory_text: I saw six Apache helicopters approaching and landing between us and the border, blocking the way and kicking up dust that made it hard to see.

grounded_facts: General Horn intervenes with Iraqi command, preventing the execution of the Shiites and securing their release.
memories.memory_text: I watched as General Horn stepped forward and spoke with the Iraqi general, stopping the execution and getting the Shiites released—I saw them walk across the border to safety while I stood there in handcuffs.

grounded_facts: A group of American soldiers and Shiite refugees attempt to cross the Iraqi border into Iran, culminating in a confrontation with U.S. military forces.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the group trying to cross the border with Archie and Doc, along with the Shiite refugees, and I remember being stopped and taken into custody by U.S. forces while the refugees were eventually released.

grounded_facts: Despite the arrests, U.S. soldiers express admiration by whistling and clapping for Archie, Troy, and Doc.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there in handcuffs with Archie and Doc, watching the border, when I heard whistling and clapping—then saw all the U.S. soldiers cheering for us even though we were under arrest, and I raised my cuffed hands to wave back.

grounded_facts: After crossing the border, Imam and his daughter wave to the arrested trio as a gesture of gratitude.
memories.memory_text: After the Shiites crossed the border, I saw Imam and his daughter wave at us, and I raised my cuffed hands to wave back along with Archie and Doc.

grounded_facts: A workday scene at Troy's carpet business where employees carry out tasks under his direction.
Troy directs workers in handling carpet rolls, asserting managerial authority.
memories.memory_text: I directed my workers as they carried out the big rolls of carpet, making sure everything ran smoothly at my business.

grounded_facts: Troy uses a respiratory inhaler, indicating a health condition requiring medical management.
memories.memory_text: I used my inhaler during the day because I need it to manage my breathing, especially when I'm active at work.

memories.memory_text: I expressed frustration to Havichon that he took just a watch from the conflict, when there's 700 million in gold hidden in Saddam's bunkers—I told him finding it could get us out of this mess, but we both knew the real challenge was locating it.

grounded_facts: CNN reporter Bill Smithson attempts to film a story about American troops celebrating in the Iraqi desert, interacting with soldiers and military personnel amid chaotic and rowdy conditions.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill Smithson trying to film a story about the troops celebrating while the sand blew in his face, and when he asked me to stop it, I told him I couldn't control the weather—he kept insisting I be his guide, not his producer.

grounded_facts: Archie refuses to assist Bill Smithson with his reporting, deflecting responsibility and asserting his role as guide rather than producer.
memories.memory_text: I refused to help Bill with his reporting when he asked, telling him I couldn't stop the sand and steering him toward covering Saddam instead, because I'm his guide, not his producer.

grounded_facts: Archie walks off with Cathy Daitch, a young reporter, signaling a shift in focus away from Bill Smithson’s filming.
memories.memory_text: I walked off with Cathy Daitch, a young reporter, shifting my focus away from Bill Smithson’s filming.

grounded_facts: A private and urgent conversation between Archie Gates and Cathy Daitch in a television truck during the day, following a sexual encounter, where intelligence about a map and the gold is discussed.
memories.memory_text: After we finished in the television truck, I stayed on the floor catching my breath while Cathy got dressed, and then she asked me to help her find a guy named Barlow who might know something about the gold.

grounded_facts: Cathy asks Archie to help her locate a man named Barlow who might have information about the gold, presenting it as a potentially unreliable lead.
memories.memory_text: Cathy told me it might be just another bullshit lead, but she asked me to help her locate a man named Barlow who could have information about the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie discovers that a map of Saddam's bunkers may have been retrieved from a prisoner's body, possibly hidden in a bodily orifice, which could lead to information about the gold.
memories.memory_text: Cathy told me they got a map of Saddam's bunkers from a prisoner's body—maybe from his head, ear, ass, or even his dick—and that it might lead to the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie expresses disbelief and seeks clarification about how the map was retrieved from a prisoner, repeating the phrase to emphasize shock.
memories.memory_text: When Cathy said they got a map out of a prisoner's head, I couldn't believe it and asked her, 'Out of a prisoner's head?' and then again, 'Out of a guy's dick?' because it sounded insane.

grounded_facts: Archie is forcibly taken from the truck by two MPs while his pants are around his ankles, interrupting the conversation.
memories.memory_text: I was yanked out of the truck by two MPs while my pants were still around my ankles, cutting off our conversation mid-sentence.

grounded_facts: Military police briefly apprehend Cathy for violating code 37D but let her go without further consequences.
memories.memory_text: I saw the MPs grab Cathy for violating code 37D, but they let her go without any real consequences.

grounded_facts: A media operation at a television truck turns into a site of conflict between Major Archie Gates and senior military officials.

grounded_facts: Archie challenges the Generals about the lack of meaningful victory and unfair recognition after the war, expressing anger and disillusionment.
memories.memory_text: I confronted the Generals, asking them what we even fought for, seeing how unfairly recognition was handed out after the war—I felt angry and disillusioned by the whole thing.

grounded_facts: General Horn reminds Archie that he is now a general and cannot be spoken to disrespectfully.

memories.memory_text: I leaned in close to General Horn and whispered 'Fuuuuuck yooouuuu, Ronnnnn,' knowing I was defying both his rank and everything military decorum stands for.

grounded_facts: Archie gives unmarked Marine uniforms to the group to adopt a new identity.
memories.memory_text: I handed out unmarked Marine uniforms to the group because we needed to become something new to survive.

grounded_facts: Archie presses the group to name the most important thing in life, rejecting their answers until asserting that 'necessity' is the true answer.
memories.memory_text: I asked the group what they thought was the most important thing in life, and when they said 'respect' and questioned me back, I told them it was necessity — that necessity shapes everything, like why we can't take out Saddam and why he'll have to eliminate the Shiites to stay in power.

grounded_facts: Archie expresses his belief that war should be a precise tool for life, not indiscriminate destruction, and frames their mission in terms of necessity.
memories.memory_text: I shared with the group that war should be a precise tool to give life by stopping evil, not about indiscriminate bombing, and that I learned to use violence carefully and surgically — a belief I still hold even though the current war effort ignores it.

grounded_facts: After regrouping and re-equipping, the group agrees to proceed to another bunker to continue their mission.
memories.memory_text: I saw the group was ready, so I pointed out that they hadn't touched us because they're scared of us, and with time on our side, I said we should try another bunker — and I could see they agreed when Conrad said 'Let's do it' and Joker said 'Rock and roll.'

grounded_facts: Troy refuses to wear the Marine uniform, citing fear of being injured after the war and concern for his family.
memories.memory_text: I remember Troy refusing to put on the uniform, saying he couldn't risk getting hurt after the war because he has a family to think about.

grounded_facts: Troy initially refuses to wear the Marine uniform due to personal risk, but later agrees under the logic of necessity and puts on Kevlar.
memories.memory_text: I remembered how Troy initially refused to wear the Marine uniform, saying it wasn't worth the risk to his family, but later I saw him agree and put on Kevlar, telling us it was just a necessity.

grounded_facts: The Hummer arrives rapidly at the entrance of an underground bunker in a village piazza, marking the start of a military intervention.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Hummer race into the village piazza and skid to a stop at the bunker entrance, marking the start of our intervention.

grounded_facts: Archie Gates uses a megaphone to order Iraqi soldiers to surrender their weapons.
memories.memory_text: I used the megaphone to order the Iraqi soldiers to put down their weapons, asserting our control as U.S. Marines.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc verbally command the Iraqi soldiers to drop their weapons during confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Troy and Doc shout at the Iraqi soldiers to drop their weapons as they moved in with their pistols drawn.

grounded_facts: A military encounter initiated by U.S. Marines upon arriving at an Iraqi village bunker, involving commands, weapon confrontation, and capture of local soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the full encounter unfold at the bunker—our arrival, my command, Troy and Doc confronting the soldiers, and their eventual capture.

grounded_facts: Troy and Doc force two Iraqi soldiers to drop their weapons, then subdue and handcuff them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Troy and Doc force the two Iraqi soldiers to the ground, disarm them, and handcuff them after the standoff.

grounded_facts: Vig issues a verbal threat toward an Iraqi soldier named Abdul, warning of lethal consequences.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig shout a threat at an Iraqi soldier named Abdul, warning him not to resist or he’d be shot.

grounded_facts: Doc subdues and restrains an Iraqi soldier who attempted to flee upon seeing the approaching team.
memories.memory_text: I saw an Iraqi soldier run away when he spotted us in the corridor, but I kept moving forward with Troy right behind me, and then I heard Doc take him down and cuff him.

grounded_facts: Archie kicks open a door and enters a room in the bunker, initiating the team's movement into a new space.
memories.memory_text: I kicked open the door and went in, leading the team into the next room with Troy right behind me.

grounded_facts: Archie declares the U.S. Marines' authority to confiscate stolen Kuwaiti materials under the Safwan cease-fire agreement.
memories.memory_text: I declared that by the Safwan cease-fire agreement, the U.S. Marines had the authority to confiscate all stolen Kuwaiti materials.

grounded_facts: Doc strikes a resisting Iraqi with his pistol, causing it to fire accidentally, prompting everyone to duck except Archie.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc hit a resisting Iraqi with his pistol, and it went off accidentally, making everyone else duck—but I stayed still.

grounded_facts: Archie criticizes Doc for hitting someone with a pistol, which caused an accidental discharge.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc smack an Iraqi with his pistol, which went off accidentally, so I told him never to hit anyone with his pistol.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Captain offers Archie a Cuisinart as a gift, possibly to appease or bribe him.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Captain offer me a Cuisinart, saying 'For wife,' but I didn't want it since I'm not married.

grounded_facts: Doc punches the resistant Iraqi twice in the head, causing him to cry.
memories.memory_text: I watched Doc punch the Iraqi twice in the head when he kept resisting, and the man started to cry.

grounded_facts: Archie demands to know the location of gold from the Iraqi Captain, threatening lethal consequences.
memories.memory_text: I demanded the location of the gold from the Captain, telling him to talk so we wouldn't have to kill him.

grounded_facts: Troy identifies and points to a narrow door leading to another room, prompting Archie to kick it open.
memories.memory_text: I saw Troy point to a narrow door and say there was another room, so I kicked the door open to check it out.

grounded_facts: U.S. Marines storm and secure an Iraqi bunker containing looted goods and personnel.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed my team storm and secure the bunker, with Doc disarming the Iraqis and me kicking open a hidden door after Troy pointed it out.

grounded_facts: Archie physically assaults the Iraqi Sergeant and takes his pistol after pulling a cable from the water box.
Archie backhands the Iraqi Sergeant and steps on his wrist to disarm him.
memories.memory_text: I walked over, pulled the cable from the water box, backhanded the Iraqi Sergeant so hard he flew into the corner, then stepped on his wrist and took his pistol.

grounded_facts: The Interrogator downplays the presence of the Shiite detainees and claims they are an internal Iraqi issue.
memories.memory_text: The Interrogator told me these Shiite detainees were an internal Iraqi issue and said they'd take them outside so it wouldn't bother me.

grounded_facts: An active interrogation involving torture of a Shiite prisoner using electric shock in water, with other detainees present.
memories.memory_text: I saw a naked Shiite man in glasses sitting in a shallow box of water, shaking as he was being tortured with electric shocks while other detainees were present.

grounded_facts: Ten Shiite detainees, including women and children, are forced out of the room through a rear door by the disarmed Iraqi Sergeant under orders from the Interrogator.
memories.memory_text: I saw the disarmed Iraqi Sergeant push the Shiite detainees out through a rear door.

grounded_facts: After disarming the sergeant and witnessing the removal of detainees, Archie points his pistol at the Interrogator and demands to be taken to the basement.
Archie points his pistol at the Interrogator's face and demands to be taken to the basement.
memories.memory_text: I disarmed the sergeant, saw the detainees being removed, and then I pointed my pistol at the Interrogator's face and told him to take us to the basement.

grounded_facts: Archie and the group arrive at Bunker Number Two after descending cement stairs.
memories.memory_text: I ran down several narrow sets of cement stairs with the group to arrive at Bunker Number Two.

grounded_facts: Iraqi Captain expresses fear that Saddam will execute him over the situation.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Iraqi Captain say that Saddam would shoot him dead over the situation.

grounded_facts: Interrogator claims Saddam is more concerned about the Shiite than the gold.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Interrogator say that Saddam worries more about the Shiite than the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie enters through the door, followed by the Iraqi Interrogator and Captain, proceeding into the next area.
memories.memory_text: I went through the door, with the Iraqi Interrogator and Captain following behind me as we moved into the next area.

grounded_facts: Archie points his pistol at the Iraqi Captain and asserts ownership over the stolen Kuwaiti assets.
memories.memory_text: I put my pistol in the Iraqi Captain's face and told him that everything he took from Kuwait now belongs to us, making it clear we were in control.

grounded_facts: After Doc and Troy pocket jewelry from the suitcases, Archie orders them to return it, enforcing the plan to take only gold.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc and Troy pocketing jewelry, so I ordered them to return it; I had to make sure we only took gold, just like the plan required.

grounded_facts: Archie instructs Doc (and by extension Troy) to return the jewelry they stole, insisting on sticking to the original plan of taking only gold.
memories.memory_text: I told Doc to put the jewelry back and stick to the plan—gold only—because that’s what we agreed on, and I meant to keep it that way.

grounded_facts: Troy bets Doc a Lexus that Lexus makes a convertible, sparking a brief humorous exchange.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Troy said he'd get a fleet of Lexus convertibles, and Doc told him Lexus doesn't make one, so Troy bet him a Lexus they do, and Doc accepted the bet, saying the car wouldn't be a convertible.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Troy discover that multiple Louis Vuitton suitcases contain bricks of gold, each weighing five kilos, with sixty bricks per suitcase, leading to a total estimate of thirty million dollars.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc open a suitcase and freeze, so I looked over and saw it was filled with five-kilo gold bricks—sixty in each Louis Vuitton case—and after checking them all with Troy and Doc, I realized we were looking at around thirty million dollars' worth.

grounded_facts: The suitcases rip apart when being carried, spilling gold bars due to insufficient tensile strength, revealing that the gold was not transported in these suitcases originally.
memories.memory_text: I saw the suitcase rip apart when we were carrying it, spilling gold everywhere, and I realized we couldn't use these bags to move the gold — they didn't get it here like this originally.

grounded_facts: A group of soldiers inspects a series of Louis Vuitton suitcases in a bunker, uncovering vast quantities of gold bricks, leading to shock, conflict, and logistical reassessment.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Louis Vuitton suitcases filled with silverware, jewelry, and watches, and when we opened the larger ones, I couldn't believe it—each was packed with sixty gold bricks; I calculated ten suitcases would be worth thirty million dollars, and I realized we couldn't carry the gold in those bags because they weren't strong enough, especially after one ripped open and spilled the bars.

grounded_facts: The group gathers in the bunker basement to pack gold bars into Louis Vuitton bags, discuss risks, and plan logistics.
memories.memory_text: I remember pacing in the bunker basement while Troy and Doc packed gold bars into Louis Vuitton bags, and I told them it felt crazy to take it all, but also crazy to leave any behind.

grounded_facts: Archie reveals the full international smuggling route for the gold involving French Special Forces, oil barrels, and multiple transit points.
memories.memory_text: I revealed the full route to them—I told them about my friend in French Special Forces who'd hide the gold in oil barrels, get it to Yanbu, then ship it via a Turkish boat up the Red Sea and transfer to a French boat bound for Baltimore.

grounded_facts: Troy, supported by Doc, pressures Archie to reveal the shipping plan, showing growing tension and distrust.
memories.memory_text: I felt the pressure when Troy and Doc both demanded I tell them how the gold would be handled, insisting I reveal the plan right then.

grounded_facts: The group decides they need a trailer to transport the gold bars because the hat boxes won't fit in the Humvee.
memories.memory_text: I realized we couldn't fit the hat boxes in the Humvee, so I said we needed a trailer to carry the gold.

grounded_facts: Troy takes action to secure a trailer by agreeing to contact U-Haul in Karbala.
memories.memory_text: I saw Troy agree to call U-Haul in Karbala to check what trailers they had available.

grounded_facts: After agreeing on the need for a trailer, Archie assigns Troy the task of contacting U-Haul in Karbala.
memories.memory_text: I assigned Troy the task of contacting U-Haul in Karbala, telling him to see what he could get.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and the Interrogator are moving up the bunker's narrow cement staircase while carrying Vuitton cases, indicating urgency or evacuation.
memories.memory_text: I was moving up the narrow cement staircase in the bunker with Doc and the Interrogator, carrying Vuitton cases, and it felt like we were in a rush to evacuate.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major warmly greets and embraces the Interrogator, signaling alliance or familiarity.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Major warmly greet and embrace the Interrogator, showing they had some kind of alliance or history.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major salutes Archie, acknowledging his status or role in the operation.
memories.memory_text: The Iraqi Major saluted me, acknowledging my role in the operation and showing me respect as a fellow officer.

grounded_facts: Archie and the Iraqi Major confirm the transfer of Kuwaiti gold, indicating a mutual understanding that Saddam cannot retain it.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed with the Iraqi Major that we would take the Kuwaiti gold, making it clear that Saddam couldn't hold onto it any longer.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major offers help to load the cargo, which Archie declines.
memories.memory_text: I declined the Iraqi Major's offer to help load the cargo, telling him we could do it ourselves, even though his men were ready to assist.

grounded_facts: Archie notices blood on an Iraqi soldier's knuckles and wrists, confirming their recent physical involvement in violence.
memories.memory_text: I saw blood on an Iraqi soldier's knuckles and wrists when I looked at his hands, and it confirmed to me they had been recently involved in violence.

grounded_facts: Archie and Doc witness soldiers beating Shiites and wounded civilians on the ground, leading to a shift in their awareness of the local conflict.
memories.memory_text: I saw Iraqi soldiers beating Shiites and wounded civilians on the ground, and noticed blood on the soldiers' hands from the violence.

grounded_facts: A group prepares to leave Bunker Number Two with stolen luggage and gold, amid ongoing conflict and military presence.
memories.memory_text: I helped carry the stolen luggage out of Bunker Number Two and loaded it onto the ox cart, then told the others it was time to leave.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers pull a Shiite woman from a group, stand her in an open area, and shoot her dead, revealing she had been raped.
memories.memory_text: I watched as the Iraqi soldiers pulled a woman from the group, stood her in an open area, and shot her dead—I could see she had been raped.

grounded_facts: The group attempts to load luggage into vehicles for departure from Bunker Number Two.
The overloaded cart collapses into a pile of broken wood, spilling the Vuitton bags onto the ground, one rolling through a pool of blood.
memories.memory_text: I got out of the Humvee and watched as the overloaded cart collapsed, spilling the luggage onto the ground, one bag rolling through a pool of blood, and I heard Troy remind me to stick to the plan.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi Major rejects Archie's offer to trade gold for the release of the Shiite prisoners, citing fear of Saddam's retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I offered the Iraqi Major gold to let the Shiite prisoners go, but he told me Saddam would kill him if he let them go, so the deal was off.

grounded_facts: Archie orders Troy to cover him as he moves to intervene in the violence.
memories.memory_text: I told Troy and the others to cover me as I moved in to stop the execution—I had to make sure they heard me, so I repeated the order.

grounded_facts: Archie instructs Vig not to fire unnecessarily and reminds him of the medical consequences of bullet wounds.
memories.memory_text: I told Vig to hold his fire and not take unnecessary shots, reminding him we both know what bullets do to vital organs.

grounded_facts: An Iraqi soldier attacks the Man In Glasses with a knife after grabbing the Girl by the hair; the man is cut but not lethally.
memories.memory_text: I saw an Iraqi soldier grab the girl by the hair and attack the man with glasses with a knife; I remember the man got cut, but not fatally, as I moved toward them.

grounded_facts: Archie confronts the Iraqi soldiers, disarms the knife-wielding soldier, and rescues the Man In Glasses and the Girl.
memories.memory_text: I stepped in, grabbed the soldier's wrist to stop the knife, took him down with a choke hold, swept his legs, pinned him, threw his gun away, then helped the man in glasses and the girl up and moved them to safety by the Humvee.

grounded_facts: A firefight erupts between American and Iraqi forces after the Iraqi Major injures Archie and Iraqi 6 shoots him; multiple casualties occur on both sides.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi Major lunge at me, and when I pushed his rifle down, it went off and hit his leg—he screamed in pain. Then Iraqi 6 shot me in the lower left arm, and I felt the bullet tear through muscle. I saw Troy fire back and drop Iraqi 6, then bullets hit Troy and Doc started shooting. I watched tracer rounds rip through more Iraqis, and in that moment, I jammed my pistol under the Major’s chin and fired—I saw his head explode from the shot.

grounded_facts: A group of Shiite prisoners, including a woman and a man with a girl, are detained and abused by Iraqi soldiers at Bunker Number Two.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Iraqi soldiers pull the Shiite woman from the group and execute her, and later I looked down at the dead Iraqi Major, my face lightly splattered with blood.

grounded_facts: After the shootout, surviving Iraqi soldiers drop their weapons and surrender to the Americans.
memories.memory_text: I saw the surviving Iraqi soldiers drop their weapons and raise their hands in surrender after the firefight.

grounded_facts: Archie orders the Shiite prisoners to be placed in the Humvee, effectively rescuing them from execution.
memories.memory_text: I ordered the Shiite prisoners to be put in the Humvee to get them out of harm's way and stop their execution.

grounded_facts: Archie demands compliance from Troy using direct and forceful language after Troy questions the order.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie demands compliance from Troy using direct and forceful language after Troy questions the order.

grounded_facts: Archie overrides Troy's objection and insists on making space in the vehicles for the Shiite prisoners, signaling a shift in mission priority to rescue.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Archie overrides Troy's objection and insists on making space in the vehicles for the Shiite prisoners, signaling a shift in mission priority to rescue.

grounded_facts: Doc challenges Troy's resistance to rescuing the Shiites by asking him to imagine being in their position.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Doc challenges Troy's resistance to rescuing the Shiites by asking him to imagine being in their position.

grounded_facts: Troy counters Doc's moral appeal by pointing to his bullet-stopped Kevlar, emphasizing personal risk and survival.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Troy counters Doc's moral appeal by pointing to his bullet-stopped Kevlar, emphasizing personal risk and survival.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi tank's turret becomes stuck, preventing it from firing, which reduces the immediate threat to the fleeing Americans.
memories.memory_text: I saw the tank's turret whine and get stuck in place, and an Iraqi soldier gestured at it while another tried pushing it, which meant they couldn't fire on us and gave us a chance to get away.

grounded_facts: An approaching Iraqi tank and rocket-launcher truck disrupt the Americans' escape attempt, creating immediate threat.
memories.memory_text: I heard an approaching tank and turned to see it rolling toward us down a narrow street, followed by a truck with a rocket launcher, which made our escape attempt suddenly much more dangerous.

grounded_facts: Doc treats Archie's gunshot wound in his lower left arm with disinfectant and bandages it.
memories.memory_text: I felt intense pain as Doc cleaned my gunshot wound in my lower left arm with disinfectant and then bandaged it.

grounded_facts: The tank is observed turning, likely preparing to target the convoy.
memories.memory_text: I saw the tank turning and asked what it was doing, then heard someone say it was lining us up, so I realized it was likely preparing to target the convoy.

grounded_facts: Archie tells Vig to remain on the road to avoid danger.
memories.memory_text: I told Vig to stay on the road to avoid danger while he was driving.

grounded_facts: While searching for his gas mask, Vig loses control and drives the Humvee off the road into a minefield.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig reach behind him for his gas mask while driving, lost control, and veered off the road into a minefield—I saw the mines ahead and realized we were in immediate danger.

grounded_facts: Upon spotting the mine, Archie and others jump out of the moving Humvee to escape imminent explosion.
The unmanned Humvee travels forward and triggers a landmine, causing a violent explosion.
memories.memory_text: I spotted the mine and jumped out of the moving Humvee, and I saw it trigger the explosion just after we got clear.

grounded_facts: Doc gives his gas mask to the Shiite Man in Glasses after seeing Archie help the Little Girl.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc take off his mask and give it to the Shiite Man in Glasses after he saw me help the Little Girl.

grounded_facts: Archie gives his gas mask to the Little Girl with arm casts; Doc gives his mask to the Shiite Man in Glasses after seeing this.
memories.memory_text: I gave my gas mask to the Little Girl with arm casts to protect her from the gas.

grounded_facts: Vig suffers shrapnel injury to his right eye; Doc retrieves and returns his glasses and helps him cover his face.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig get hit in the right eye by shrapnel and start groping in the sand for his glasses; I watched Doc pick them up and hand them back to him, then help him cover his face as blood streamed down.

grounded_facts: Archie physically stops Doc from injecting himself, correcting his misdiagnosis of the gas.
Archie identifies the gas as CS gas, not sarin or mustard, relieving Doc and clarifying the threat level.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Doc's hand to stop him from injecting himself because I knew it wasn't sarin—we'd have been dead by then—and I told him it was just CS gas, like tear gas times ten.

grounded_facts: The group observes black-robed figures leading the Shiites to a hidden tunnel entrance in the desert mound.
memories.memory_text: I saw the black-robed figures leading the Shiites toward a low tunnel entrance in the desert mound, and I remember feeling disoriented as they disappeared inside.

grounded_facts: Doc grabs Vig and tells him to get into the tunnel, attempting to force compliance for survival.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc grab Vig and pull him toward the tunnel, yelling at him to get in.

grounded_facts: Vig jerks his arm away from Doc and refuses to enter the tunnel, calling out for Troy.
memories.memory_text: I watched Vig jerk his arm away from Doc and call out for Troy, refusing to go into the tunnel.

grounded_facts: Vig and Doc engage in a violent physical fight after Vig resists entering the tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig and Doc start fighting violently after Vig resisted, punching each other and falling to the ground.

grounded_facts: Archie calls out and searches for Barlow in the haze, showing concern for his missing comrade.
memories.memory_text: I called out for Barlow and searched for him in the haze, worried about where he'd gone.

grounded_facts: Archie chokes and vomits while searching for Troy in the haze.
memories.memory_text: I started choking and couldn't hold it together—I ended up vomiting into the sand while I was looking for Troy.

grounded_facts: A mysterious group of thirty black-robed figures appears in the desert haze, leading the Shiites and then forcibly guiding the main characters toward a hidden tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I was in the haze with Doc, trying to make sense of things, when thirty black-robed figures appeared and started forcing us toward the tunnel—I dropped my bag, pointed my gun, but they grabbed me and pulled me back to the entrance against my will.

grounded_facts: Black-robed figures physically drag Archie, Doc, and Vig into the tunnel against initial resistance.
memories.memory_text: I was disoriented and trying to find Troy when black-robed figures grabbed me and pulled me back toward the tunnel, forcing me inside even though I resisted.

grounded_facts: A chaotic situation in a low tunnel filled with gas, where survivors struggle to breathe and tend to injuries.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the low tunnel, choking on gas and seeing people struggle to breathe while lanterns swung and buckets of oiled rags were passed around.

grounded_facts: After being accused of making a choice to leave Troy, Archie screams back that he had no choice, expressing guilt and moral anguish.
memories.memory_text: When Vig accused me of choosing to leave Troy behind, I screamed at him that I had no choice, I really had no fucking choice—I couldn't have done anything else.

grounded_facts: Archie asserts that he cannot abandon Troy's body after the violent incident, emphasizing moral responsibility over escape with gold.
memories.memory_text: I told Vig I can't just walk away from what happened to Troy and take the gold like nothing's wrong—if he can, then I hope he dies right now.

grounded_facts: Archie tends to Vig's wounded eye socket using a bandage provided by Doc, indicating continued care despite conflict.
memories.memory_text: I used a bandage that Doc handed me to cover Vig's wounded eye socket, doing what I could to help even though everything was falling apart around us.

grounded_facts: Vig counters Archie's moral stance by asking what choice Troy has now, challenging the futility or hypocrisy of Archie's position.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Vig, 'What about Troy? What choice does he have now?'—challenging my moral stance and making me question the futility of my position.

grounded_facts: Archie emerges from a mound in the desert and leads Doc and Vig toward a strange minaret.
memories.memory_text: I climbed out of a desert mound, squinted in the sunlight, and led Doc and Vig toward a strange minaret.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Vig enter the ancient minaret through its old wooden doorway.
memories.memory_text: I entered the ancient minaret with Doc and Vig through its old wooden doorway.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Vig make eye contact with a line of injured children upon entering the minaret hallway, establishing mutual awareness.
memories.memory_text: I made eye contact with a line of injured children as Doc, Vig, and I entered the minaret hallway, and in that moment, we all recognized each other.

grounded_facts: Archie endures painful treatment as a cleric shoots alcohol into his infected wound.
memories.memory_text: I gritted my teeth and screamed as a cleric shot alcohol into my infected wound, the pain almost unbearable.

grounded_facts: Vig expresses remorse for hitting Doc earlier, citing fear for Troy, and reaches out for reconciliation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig tell Doc he was sorry for hitting him, saying he was scared for Troy and wanted to make things right.

grounded_facts: Vig reaches out his hand to Doc as a gesture of apology and reconciliation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig reach out his hand to Doc, and after a pause, Doc took it — they stayed silent, but it meant they were reconciled.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Vig inspect the remaining gold bars in the Vuitton suitcases.
memories.memory_text: I decided we should check the suitcases, so I joined Doc and Vig to inspect how much gold was left inside the Vuitton cases.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, and Vig inspect the Vuitton suitcases and confirm the current amount of gold.
memories.memory_text: I checked the Vuitton suitcases with Doc and Vig, counted the gold, and figured we had 92 cases left—five bars each, so 460 total—worth a million dollars. It wasn't bad for a disaster, but only if we could find Barlow, get back before dark, and not get caught.

grounded_facts: Despite risks, Doc commits to joining Archie in rescuing Barlow.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc say 'I'm in' after I laid out the risks, so I knew he was committing to come with me to rescue Barlow despite everything.

grounded_facts: Imam accuses Archie of stealing the gold rather than acting under military orders.
memories.memory_text: I was accused of stealing the gold instead of acting under military orders.

grounded_facts: Imam Katar demands fifteen suitcases of gold to guide the group to Oasis Bunker and provide fighters.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Imam Katar demanded fifteen suitcases of gold to guide us to Oasis Bunker and provide fighters.

grounded_facts: Archie and Imam Katar finalize an agreement: ten suitcases of gold in exchange for guides, fighters, and partial return of gold for Iranian border crossing.
memories.memory_text: I finalized a deal with Imam Katar: ten suitcases of gold in exchange for guides, fighters, and five suitcases returned to help us cross the Iranian border.

grounded_facts: Doc attempts to incentivize someone to guide them to Oasis Bunker by offering gold.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc pull out gold bars and dump a suitcase of them while asking who would take us to Oasis Bunker.

grounded_facts: Archie, Doc, Vig, and Imam Katar negotiate terms for a joint mission to rescue Barlow from Oasis Bunker.
memories.memory_text: I negotiated with Imam Katar and the others, trying to arrange a joint mission to rescue Barlow from Oasis Bunker while discussing how we'd get the choppers and handle the gold.

grounded_facts: A group of injured people, including Archie, Vig, and Doc, receive medical care from Shiite clerics in a minaret room.
memories.memory_text: I was in a minaret room with Vig, Doc, and others, all of us injured and receiving medical care from Shiite clerics while I endured my own treatment.

grounded_facts: Archie asks if anything was saved from the Humvee, seeking information about available resources.
memories.memory_text: I asked Doc if we saved anything from the Humvee because I needed to know what resources were available.

grounded_facts: Archie looks at Doc as if expressing disappointment or sarcasm upon seeing only a bag was saved from the Humvee.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Doc with disappointment when he showed me only a bag was saved from the Humvee.

grounded_facts: Archie constructs a bomb using a football wrapped in plastic explosive, embedded with nails and a fuse; a second identical bomb has already been made.
memories.memory_text: I constructed a bomb using a football wrapped in plastic explosive, embedded with nails and a fuse, and I already made one just like it.

grounded_facts: Archie issues a formal military command for anyone inside the truck to surrender with hands up.
memories.memory_text: I issued a command for anyone in the truck to come out with their hands up, asserting control as the leader of the group.

grounded_facts: Vig accidentally fires his pistol, revealing that the Iraqi military truck is a decoy made of canvas.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig's pistol fire accidentally, and I watched the truck collapse like a deflated balloon, realizing it was just a canvas decoy.

grounded_facts: Imam informs the group about a place where deserters might have vehicles.
Imam proposes a location full of deserters where they might find a vehicle.

memories.memory_text: I politely declined the offer by saying 'No, thank you,' as I had no intention of accepting the monkey as food.

memories.memory_text: I was embraced by an Iraqi soldier after he congratulated me on Bush removing Saddam, and I looked to Imam in that moment, feeling awkward.

memories.memory_text: I asked Imam to explain to the Iraqi soldiers that we needed a vehicle of some kind, relying on him to translate my request clearly.

memories.memory_text: I heard Doc ask if the convertible was a Lexus, and the Iraqi soldier responded that it was an Infiniti, not a Lexus, laughing as he clarified—making it clear these vehicles were valuable and not to be given away freely.

grounded_facts: A gathering in the bunker garage where American soldiers discover stolen luxury vehicles and attempt to rally Iraqi deserters for a joint cause.
memories.memory_text: I stood in the bunker garage trying to rally the Iraqi deserters, positioning myself as a unifying leader for a joint rebellion, but their cheers only came when money was mentioned—not freedom.

grounded_facts: The group discovers an underground garage filled with luxury cars taken from Kuwait.
memories.memory_text: I entered the underground garage with Doc and Vig and saw the collection of luxury cars stolen from Kuwait, realizing immediately the scale of what we had stumbled upon.

grounded_facts: Despite Archie's speech, the Iraqi soldier reiterates they cannot give away the cars.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Iraqi soldier tell me they couldn't give the car.

grounded_facts: Archie delivers a passionate speech to unite the group and inspire rebellion against Saddam.
Archie attempts to inspire unity and rebellion among the Iraqis by invoking shared values and American support.
memories.memory_text: I delivered a passionate speech to the Iraqi soldiers, telling them we could rise up together against Saddam, and I emphasized that if they made the fight for freedom, America would follow—I walked among them, looked them in the eye, and said God bless a free Iraq, and they cheered, but then I realized we’d have to buy the cars after all.

grounded_facts: The Iraqi soldiers refuse to give the cars to the Americans, despite Archie's persuasive speech.
memories.memory_text: After my speech about fighting Saddam and rising together, I realized the Iraqi soldiers wouldn't hand over the cars, so I figured we'd have to buy them instead.

grounded_facts: The 92 Vuitton suitcases containing gold are buried in a trench and the location is marked with a stake by Archie.
memories.memory_text: I drove a stake into the ground to mark where we buried the 92 Vuitton suitcases full of gold, making sure we could find it again later.

grounded_facts: Archie explicitly links the survival of the Imam's people to the successful retrieval of all the gold, implying a threat if the mission fails.
memories.memory_text: I told the Imam that if my gold isn't here, all of it, his people won't survive.

memories.memory_text: I saw Doc and Vig take the distributor caps off the Cadillacs and the Limousine and stash them in Doc's pack so no one could use those vehicles.

memories.memory_text: I sang Bach's 'Gloria' loudly to steady myself and put my hands on Vig's shoulders, and after a moment, he joined in with me, helping us both cope with the fear.

grounded_facts: Archie uses music to soothe Vig's anxiety, physically engaging him and singing loudly to build courage.
memories.memory_text: I used music to calm Vig down, putting my hands on his shoulders and singing Bach's 'Gloria' loud to help him find his courage—we even ended up singing the chorus together.

memories.memory_text: I remember the meeting in the desert where we buried the gold, said our goodbyes, and I sang Bach's 'Gloria' with Vig to steady us both before the mission.

memories.memory_text: I saw Imam's daughter get out of the Jaguar despite him scolding her and gesturing for her to go back, and then she hugged him while staring down at Troy, looking both connected and worried.

memories.memory_text: I performed a needle decompression on Troy's chest, cutting into his upper chest near the collar bone to release trapped air, and I heard the hissing sound as the air rushed out and saw the relief on his face when he could breathe again.

grounded_facts: Archie makes a statement indicating personal fulfillment after successfully performing the procedure.
memories.memory_text: I've been waiting 18 years to get that right, and finally I did it.

memories.memory_text: I inserted an IV tube into the decompression site to keep the air from building up again and tightened the valve to stabilize the opening.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Shiite women and children gathered around Vig's body in the trunk of the Jaguar, chanting and praying as we stood there in silence.

memories.memory_text: I carefully took the pistol from Vig's clenched hand, feeling the weight of it and knowing I was now responsible for carrying on what he stood for.

memories.memory_text: I told the others, 'We're his family now,' and in that moment, I accepted the duty to see Vig's remains returned to Kajatar as he wished.

memories.memory_text: I was told the Imam offered to take Vig's body to the shrine at Kajatar in Iran.

memories.memory_text: I removed Vig's glasses, a quiet and personal moment that made his loss feel more real.

memories.memory_text: I agreed to send Vig's body to the shrine at Kajatar in Iran to honor his final wish.

memories.memory_text: I sealed the rusted oil drum after filling it with gold bars to get it ready for transport.

memories.memory_text: I estimated to Troy that he might survive about four hours if he wasn't bleeding too badly inside.

grounded_facts: Troy communicates his physical need for water.
memories.memory_text: I heard Troy say he was really thirsty, so I knew he was feeling the need for water.

memories.memory_text: I remember Doc stating there was no water anywhere in the area.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Imam that the communication system is ready and I can use it to contact my man.

grounded_facts: Doc voices concern that they will face military legal consequences.
memories.memory_text: I heard Doc say we were going to be court-martialed, and I knew he was afraid of what might happen to us.

memories.memory_text: I used my radio hooked up to a car battery to keep calling Tar Baby with my Brer Rabbit call sign, trying to get a response.

memories.memory_text: I heard Walter ask if the Tar Baby goes to the briar patch when everything's OK, and I corrected him, telling him it was the other way around.

memories.memory_text: I instructed Walter over the radio to secure six personnel trucks and a Humvee, arrange for each driver to get 100K through my contact Hash, add a medavac pack to the order, and dump the reporter.

grounded_facts: Walter commits to completing the assigned mission within two hours after receiving full instructions.
memories.memory_text: I heard Walter commit to completing the mission within two hours after I gave him the full instructions.

grounded_facts: A real-time radio exchange between Walter in the desert and Archie (off-site), serving as a coordination point for mission directives.
memories.memory_text: I was on the radio with Walter in the desert, coordinating the mission—we confirmed our positions, I gave him updated orders including adding a medavac pack and dropping the reporter, and he acknowledged he’d need two hours.

grounded_facts: Doc opens a snow globe, releasing water and dollars, which drain out.
memories.memory_text: I saw Doc crack open a snow globe with pliers, and all the water and dollars drained out right away.

grounded_facts: Imam filters the water from the snow globe through a cheese cloth into an urn.
memories.memory_text: I watched Imam filter the snow globe water through a cheese cloth into an urn to clean it.

grounded_facts: Archie passes an urn to parched Shiites who drink the filtered water thirstily.
memories.memory_text: I passed the urn to the parched Shiites and watched them drink the filtered water thirstily.

memories.memory_text: I watched Imam and another Shiite hand out gold bars to the peasants waiting in line, and I saw one man take two bars and stash them in his clothes just like the others.

grounded_facts: Walter greets Troy and administers medical treatment; they exchange light-hearted remarks about protecting the free world and going home.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Walter greet Troy with a fist bump and joke about protecting the free world and going home, then offer medical help.

memories.memory_text: I felt the needle go into my arm as Doc taped the penicillin bag to my shirt, and I knew they were stabilizing me for evacuation.

memories.memory_text: Havichon sarcastically remarked that I got myself shot, and I responded dryly, then told him the bullion is buried and I’ll show him after we get everyone to the border—it’s part of the deal.

grounded_facts: Havichon asks about the location of the bullion; Archie confirms it is buried and promises to reveal it after reaching the border.
memories.memory_text: I told Havichon the bullion is buried and that I'll show him after we get the people to the border—it's part of the deal.

memories.memory_text: When Walter apologized for messing up the code, I realized we had to move out fast because they might be coming for us.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Shiite peasants piling into the trucks, and I watched Doc help Imam and his daughter get settled before we prepared to move out.

memories.memory_text: I heard the sound of approaching motors and saw a U.S. military convoy arrive, and I whistled from the front seat of the Humvee to lead the convoy out with the Shiites and the gold.

memories.memory_text: I whistled from the Humvee to signal departure, and I led the convoy as we rolled out onto the desert road toward the border.

memories.memory_text: Havichon asked me what I saw, so I told him about the opening and that it was only wide enough for us to walk through.

memories.memory_text: I noticed a narrow opening in the border while I was looking at it from the Humvee, and I realized we could walk through it, but no vehicle would fit.

memories.memory_text: I decided we'd walk the refugees to the Iranian side of the border and then return to the trucks, so I announced the plan to the team.

memories.memory_text: I figured we’d need to escort the refugees on foot since the trucks couldn’t go through, and I thought we could walk them to the border and then return to the vehicles, though I wasn’t entirely sure how the handoff would go.

grounded_facts: Troy disengages the safety on his M-16 rifle, indicating preparation for potential conflict.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Troy disengaging the safety on his M-16, getting ready in case we ran into trouble during the crossing.

memories.memory_text: I saw the U.S. drivers get out of their vehicles with rifles ready and take the safeties off, taking up a defensive posture as we prepared to move.

memories.memory_text: I told the group to make a close formation before crossing, and the Imam translated my order so everyone would understand.

grounded_facts: A coordinated movement of Shiite refugees and U.S. drivers crossing the border through a narrow opening in razor wire, carrying Vig's body and maintaining armed vigilance.
memories.memory_text: I saw the whole group moving together through the wire, Shiites carrying Vig, with all of us U.S. drivers flanking them and staying alert on both sides.

memories.memory_text: I heard the choppers first, then turned and saw six Apaches approaching — they landed right between me and the border, blocking our way and kicking up so much dust that I had to shield my eyes.

memories.memory_text: I heard Captain Van Meter yell at Troy to shut up, telling him he was fucked now and rejecting his pleas.

grounded_facts: Archie reveals the presence of stolen Kuwaiti gold bullion to General Horn, proving its recovery by the group.
memories.memory_text: I saw the MPs uncover the truck and spill the gold bars onto the sand, and I made sure General Horn saw it too — we had the stolen Kuwaiti gold, and I used that to prove we could deliver it.

grounded_facts: Archie appeals to General Horn's sense of honor and ambition to save the Shiites, offering the gold as leverage.
memories.memory_text: I appealed to General Horn's sense of honor and ambition, telling him he could return the gold and be a hero, maybe even get another star, if he'd help save the Shiites.

grounded_facts: Troy, unable to breathe due to tight restraints, has his plastic cuffs cut by a sympathetic soldier, allowing him to access his chest valve and breathe.
A U.S. soldier silently cuts Troy's cuffs, defying orders to save his life.
memories.memory_text: I was handcuffed and watching when Troy couldn't breathe because the restraints were too tight, and I saw a U.S. soldier silently cut his cuffs with a knife, which let him reach the valve on his chest and finally breathe again.

grounded_facts: Archie, Troy, and Doc are apprehended and handcuffed by U.S. Military Police upon arrival of U.S. forces.
memories.memory_text: I was grabbed by the MPs along with Troy and Doc, and we were all handcuffed while they separated us from the Shiites.

grounded_facts: General Horn intervenes with Iraqi forces, stopping the imminent execution of the Shiite refugees.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Horn fire his pistol into the air, freezing the Iraqi soldiers who were about to execute the Shiites, and then walk with Captain Van Meter to intervene directly.

grounded_facts: General Horn orders the confiscation of news cameras and tapes, suppressing documentation of the event.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Horn order the cameras turned off and the tapes taken by the MPs, shutting down any chance to document what really happened.

grounded_facts: A group of U.S. soldiers and Shiite refugees attempt to cross the Iraqi border into Iran, culminating in confrontation with U.S. military forces.
memories.memory_text: I was walking with Troy and Doc, trying to get the Shiites across the border so they could be safe, but then I saw the choppers coming and everything changed — we were grabbed by MPs, cuffed, and could only watch as the Shiites finally made it across while we were held back.

grounded_facts: Iraqi soldiers release the Shiite refugees, who then cross the border into Iran and are received by relief workers.
memories.memory_text: I watched as the Iraqi soldiers released the Shiites, who then crossed the border into Iran and were received by relief workers while Troy, Doc, and I stood there in handcuffs.

grounded_facts: Imam and his daughter wave from the Iranian side as they board a Red Crescent bus, with Archie, Troy, and Doc waving back in handcuffs.
memories.memory_text: I saw Imam and his daughter wave from the Iranian side as they boarded a Red Crescent bus, and I raised my handcuffed hands to wave back alongside Troy and Doc.

grounded_facts: U.S. soldiers begin whistling and clapping in support of Archie, Troy, and Doc despite their arrest.
memories.memory_text: Even though we were under arrest and handcuffed, I heard soldiers start whistling and clapping for us, and I raised my cuffed hands to wave back—I felt their support in that moment.

grounded_facts: Archie shows an action star how to push away the barrel of a bad guy's rifle on a film set.
memories.memory_text: I showed an action star on a film set how to push away the barrel of a bad guy's rifle while wearing sunglasses.

grounded_facts: Archie demonstrates tactical maneuvers on a Hollywood film set.
memories.memory_text: I was on a Hollywood film set, wearing sunglasses, and showed an action star how to push away the barrel of a bad guy's rifle during a scene.

memories.memory_text: I confronted Havichon about taking just a watch, telling him there's 700 million in gold out there and wondering how we could ever find Saddam's bullion.

grounded_facts: Bill Smithson asks for help with his report, but Archie minimizes the request and redirects him to focus on the celebration story.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill ask me for help with his report, but I downplayed it and told him to focus on the celebration instead.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Archie to act as his guide, not his producer, expressing irritation at Archie's editorial interference.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill to just act as his guide and not his producer, and he made it clear he didn't want me interfering editorially.

grounded_facts: Soldiers chant patriotic songs and make boastful statements directly into the camera, engaging with the reporter's presence.
American soldiers celebrate their military success with dancing, chanting, and posing for a CNN crew, expressing pride and triumph while music plays loudly.
memories.memory_text: I saw the soldiers celebrating our victory in Kuwait, dancing and chanting 'We're number one' while music played loudly, and some of them proudly sang 'Proud to Be An American' into the CNN camera.

grounded_facts: A private and intimate encounter between Archie Gates and Cathy Daitch in a television truck, which transitions into a discussion about a new lead on the gold.
memories.memory_text: I was with Cathy in the television truck, and after our intimate moment, things shifted into a more serious conversation.

grounded_facts: Cathy asks Archie to help her find a man named Barlow who may have information about the gold, based on a map allegedly retrieved from a prisoner's body.
memories.memory_text: Cathy told me I needed to help her find a man named Barlow, maybe in Company B, who might have information about the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie discovers that a map of Saddam's bunkers may have been retrieved from a prisoner's body, possibly hidden in a bodily orifice, which could lead to information about the gold.
memories.memory_text: I was told that a map of Saddam's bunkers might have been retrieved from a prisoner's body—maybe from his head, ear, ass, or even his dick—and that it could lead to the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie expresses disbelief and seeks clarification about how the map was retrieved from a prisoner's body.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't believe it and asked Cathy, 'Out of a prisoner's head?' and then again, 'Out of a guy's dick?' because the story sounded insane.

grounded_facts: Archie is forcibly taken from the truck by two MPs while his pants are around his ankles, interrupting his conversation with Cathy.
memories.memory_text: I was pulled out of the truck by two MPs while my pants were around my ankles, cutting off my conversation with Cathy.

grounded_facts: Military police briefly detain Cathy for violating code 37D by 'grinding' Major Gates.
memories.memory_text: I was present when the military police detained Cathy for violating code 37D by 'grinding' me, and I knew they were enforcing protocol against her for associating with me.

grounded_facts: General Pye cuts off Smithson's attempt to raise the gold story, asserting control over the narrative.
memories.memory_text: I saw General Pye cut off Smithson when he tried to bring up the gold story, making it clear he wouldn't allow any challenge to the official narrative.

grounded_facts: A military-coordinated media event where generals manage press access and narrative control during the Gulf War.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed how the generals managed the media event, controlling access and messaging, and I remember being told I had a prestige job in the media war while seeing how tightly they controlled everything.

grounded_facts: Archie physically confronts General Horn by grabbing his uniform collar, symbolically rejecting his rank.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed the corner of General Horn's collar, feeling the fabric between my fingers as I pulled slightly, making a point without speaking.

grounded_facts: General Horn reminds Archie that he cannot swear at him due to his higher rank.
memories.memory_text: I was told I couldn't say 'fuck you' to General Horn because he's a general now, like rank suddenly made him untouchable.

grounded_facts: Archie challenges the Generals about the lack of meaningful military victory and the unfair distribution of recognition and rewards.
memories.memory_text: I told the Generals it was ironic, what we were doing—how we claimed victory but nothing felt earned, and how the rewards went to the wrong people.

grounded_facts: Archie whispers an exaggerated, mocking 'fuck you' to General Horn after being told he can't say it due to rank.
memories.memory_text: I leaned in close to Horn's face and whispered 'Fuuuuuck yooouuuu, Ronnnnn'—a slow, mocking version of the words I wasn't allowed to say outright.

grounded_facts: Archie confronts Troy for control of the map, using psychological pressure and rank implication.
memories.memory_text: I fixed my gaze on Troy, walked up, reached under the table, and took the map—he didn’t let go at first, so we stood there, both holding it, staring each other down until I asked, 'May I look at the goddamn map?'

grounded_facts: Archie uses infrared light to reveal a hidden map on the document, showing a different set of bunkers farther west.
memories.memory_text: I used infrared light to reveal a hidden map on the document, and I saw that it still showed three bunkers but farther west, which I pointed out to the others.

grounded_facts: A meeting in the captain's tent where a hidden map is revealed and a gold heist plan is discussed.
memories.memory_text: I was in the captain's tent where I demanded to see the map they were hiding, and after some tension with Troy, I used infrared light to reveal a hidden map showing bunkers near Karbala farther west, and we discussed the risks of taking a Humvee and the plan to go after the gold.

grounded_facts: Archie proposes a mission to steal Kuwaiti bullion from remote bunkers, framing it as a low-risk, high-reward operation.
memories.memory_text: I told the team about the Kuwaiti bullion hidden in remote bunkers, emphasizing how easy it would be to take from a single location and how much it could net us—kilos of gold, $50,000 per brick—enough to leave our military lives behind, especially since the Iraqi army was already beaten and surrendering everywhere.

grounded_facts: Archie formally takes control of the group, reassigning Walter and redirecting Bill Smithson's mission.
memories.memory_text: I formally took command of the group, told them they were under my authority, and had them salute me to establish order and leadership.

grounded_facts: Archie tells Walter that his captain will be detained, allowing Walter to leave his unit.
Archie informs Walter that his captain will be detained by an ally, enabling Walter to leave his unit.
memories.memory_text: I told Walter that his captain would be detained by a friend of mine, which would allow him to leave his unit and join the mission.

grounded_facts: Archie directly threatens Vig with death if he discloses the plan, effectively silencing him.
memories.memory_text: I told Vig directly that if he talks to anyone about this plan, I'll kill him.

grounded_facts: Archie warns Vig that he will be killed if he speaks about the plan, causing Vig's smile to fade.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vig's smile fade when I gave him that warning, and I knew he understood I wasn't bluffing.

grounded_facts: Troy claims he threw the ball with a higher arc to make it easier for Doc to hit.
memories.memory_text: I heard Troy say he threw the ball with a higher arc to make it easier for Doc to hit.

grounded_facts: Vig asserts that Black people make better receivers than quarterbacks, introducing racial stereotyping into the conversation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Vig say that Black people make better receivers than quarterbacks while I was driving the Humvee.

grounded_facts: Doc cites Warren Moon as an excellent Black quarterback to challenge Vig's stereotype.
memories.memory_text: I remember Doc responding to Vig by saying, 'Warren Moon is an excellent quarterback,' challenging the stereotype.

grounded_facts: A discussion about Black quarterbacks in the NFL turns into a racially charged argument among the soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the conversation escalate into a heated argument about Black quarterbacks, with Vig doubting Moon's impact, Troy telling Doc not to engage, and later affirming that there are many excellent Black quarterbacks.

grounded_facts: The group starts a shooting game in the desert, using a football as a target for rifle and pistol fire.
